sections.label: Future Economy and RIE2025 plans
sections.summary: The Government's agenda is guided by the Committee for the Future Economy report and the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government's agenda continues to be guided by the Committee for the Future Economy report released four years ago and by the more recently released Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan, amongst others.

sections.label: Capability Transfer Programme beneficiaries
sections.summary: Fewer than 970 Singaporeans have benefited from the Capability Transfer Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, I was surprised by the relatively small number of Singaporeans who have benefited from the Capability Transfer Programme, or CTP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fewer than 970 Singaporeans have benefited thus far.

sections.label: Extending Capability Transfer Programme
sections.summary: The CTP is extended until 2024, and the Minister is asked what it achieved and how much was spent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In extending the CTP until 2024, can the Minister share what has been achieved by the programme for the Singaporean worker thus far and how much money has been spent on it?

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills funding
sections.summary: An additional $5.4 billion would be allocated to a second SGUnited Jobs and Skills package, on top of $3 billion last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a similar vein, Mr Speaker, the Minister shared that an additional $5.4 billion would be allocated to a second SGUnited Jobs and Skills package, on top of the $3 billion allocated last year.

sections.label: CDC vouchers for households
sections.summary: The query concerns the announcement of $100 worth of CDC vouchers to all households for heartland shops and hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My key query in this section pertains to the announcement of the disbursement of $100 worth of Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers to all households to be used at participating heartland shops and hawker centres.

sections.label: COVID-19 Family Assistance Fund
sections.summary: Beyond Social Services' COVID-19 Family Assistance Fund committed over $3 million to more than 1,900 families, with income drops reported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Beyond Social Services launched its COVID-19 Family Assistance Fund in March 2020 and, in six months, had committed over $3 million to more than 1,900 families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Post-COVID-19, the median household income from work fell from $1,600 to $500, a 69% drop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The median per capita income fell 74% from $425 to $113, and 35% of FAF applicants saw their income drop to $0.

sections.label: Vouchers for public rental households
sections.summary: It says disbursing more assistance through vouchers and schemes from the Contingencies Fund to public rental households should be seriously considered this financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moving forward, the disbursement of additional assistance through other vouchers and schemes from the Contingencies Fund targeted at households in public rental units should be seriously considered throughout the course of this financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would also be consistent with the findings of the Government’s Emerging Stronger Conversations thus far which, after 88 conversations involving 4,400 participants, finds social support – covering issues like dignity of the less privileged, protection of vulnerable segments, and support for giving and volunteerism – ranked as the most discussed topic.

sections.label: CDC funding and voucher allocation
sections.summary: It states CDC allocations rose from $20 million to $75 million, and asks how much of the $150 million is for the scheme and its administration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government allocated $20 million to the CDCs in the Unity Budget last year and this increased to $75 million a month later in the Resilience Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This injection is equal to all the reserves of the CDCs put together, according to the CDCs' FY2018 Annual Report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the CDC vouchers, out of the $150 million being allocated to resource the latest initiative, how much is allocated for the scheme per se, and separately how much constitutes the amount allocated for the administration of the programme, as this is unclear in the Deputy Prime Minister's speech?

sections.label: Petrol duty increase timing
sections.summary: It states the decision to raise petrol duties came like an ill-timed bolt from the blue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, the decision to raise petrol duties came like an ill-timed bolt from the blue.

sections.label: Assessment of petrol duty inflation
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to confirm whether any assessment was carried out on the inflationary effect of a petrol duty rise and its impact on cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, can Minister confirm if any assessment has been carried out as to the inflationary effect of a rise in petrol duties and its impact on cost of living for Singaporeans, particularly in this economic climate?

sections.label: Scrutiny of Budget outcomes
sections.summary: It says scrutiny raises ownership and should extend to Budget outcomes and to reconsidering institutions whose roles overlap, redeploying resources to the low-income and needy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The scrutiny raises everyone's sense of ownership in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It should logically extend to the outcomes of Budget initiatives for Singapore and workers and their success in transitioning to high value-added jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They should be consistently reviewed especially since significant fiscal resources are being deployed across a number of years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The relevance of institutions whose roles and functions substantively overlap with other state agencies should also be reconsidered, with finite fiscal resources redeployed to support the low-income and needy.

sections.label: Economic contraction and support schemes
sections.summary: It states the economy contracted 5.4% in 2020 instead of an estimated 12.4%, with JSS, financing schemes, JGI and SGUnited supporting businesses and jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The economy contracted by 5.4% in 2020, instead of contracting an estimated 12.4% without the Government's support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The hefty $22.6 billion of JSS coupled with the $17 billion worth of financing schemes helped keep many businesses afloat and prevented massive job losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Under the JGI, 110,000 jobseekers were hired and another 76,000 Singaporeans were placed under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

sections.label: Household payouts and healthcare spending
sections.summary: Each household received an average of $2,000, lower income households up to $2,800, and $13.8 billion was committed to public healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: On average, each household received $2,000 while the lower income households received up to $2,800.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: On the public healthcare front, a total of $13.8 billion was committed to protect and save lives.

sections.label: Allocation to three strategic enablers
sections.summary: The Government will allocate $24 billion to invest in three strategic enablers over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In all, the Government will allocate $24 billion to invest in these three strategic enablers over the next three years.

sections.label: Special purpose borrowing for investments
sections.summary: The passage proposes funding emerging stronger-related investments through a once-off bond issuance, citing strong balance sheet, high credit ratings and low long-term interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: If the fiscal condition remains tight in this term of Government, and these are indeed time critical and worthy investments for the future, I submit that we can justify funding this emerging stronger-related investments through a special purpose borrowing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This could be a once-off bond issuance earmarked to specifically fund these economic investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: That way, we also take advantage of our very strong balance sheet and our high credit ratings where we can enjoy borrowing at zero credit cost as well as to take advantage of the low long-term interest rates.

sections.label: GST Assurance Package assurance
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister reiterated that if GST is raised, the $6 billion Assurance Package set aside in the GSTV Fund will cushion the impact for low- and middle-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In this Budget, Deputy Prime Minister reiterated the Government's assurance that should GST be raised, the $6 billion Assurance Package, which have already been set aside in the GSTV Fund, will kick in and help cushion the impact for the low- and middle-income households.

sections.label: Rise in healthcare spending
sections.summary: Healthcare spending rose from $2.2 billion ten years ago to $12 billion now, more than five times, and will continue to rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Ten years ago, healthcare spending was $2.2 billion, now it has increased more than five times to $12 billion and will continue to rise.

sections.label: GST Assurance Package cash rebates
sections.summary: The $6 billion Assurance Package will help lower and middle income families, with each adult Singaporean receiving an average of $700 to $1,600 in cash rebates over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister also reiterated that once the GST is raised, the Government will use the $6 billion Assurance Package set aside to help lower and middle income families to offset or mitigate the impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Under the Package, each adult Singaporean will receive an average of $700 to $1,600 in cash rebates over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For example, a family of four with a gross household income of about $6,000 will receive nearly $7,000 in cash rebates.

sections.label: Challenging year in fiscal management
sections.summary: The past year set precedents including the largest budget deficit, largest reserves draw for two consecutive years, and five Budgets and two Ministerial Statements to fight COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, in conclusion, the last one year has been most challenging times in our fiscal management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We set new precedents in many areas: the largest budget deficit in our history, the largest draw on our reserves for two consecutive years and, of course, five Budgets and two Ministerial Statements all in one year to fight COVID-19.

sections.label: FY2021 Budget and borrowing
sections.summary: The FY2021 Budget will be expansionary with an $11 billion deficit, and the Government intends to borrow up to $90 billion for long-term infrastructure investment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For Financial Year 2021 Budget, it will be expansionary, running up a deficit of $11 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Most significantly, the Government intends to borrow up to $90 billion to create fiscal space to press on with major and long-term infrastructure investment, despite the uncertain economic environment.

sections.label: SINGA Bonds and bond market
sections.summary: The Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act, including green infrastructure bonds, will support the development of Singapore's bond market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act or SINGA Bonds, which include green infrastructure bonds, will also support the development of Singapore’s bond market.

sections.label: Question on $90 billion debt limit
sections.summary: A speaker says borrowing would invest in a flat, and asks the Deputy Prime Minister how the $90 billion debt issuance limit was set.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We would, however, borrow to invest in our flat, to provide a long-term home for our family and an asset in our retirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Deputy Prime Minister how the $90 billion limit on debt issuance was set.

sections.label: AAA rating and GST on e-commerce
sections.summary: A speaker asks how Singapore's AAA credit rating would be impacted by borrowing, and welcomes GST extension to lower-value cross-border e-commerce transactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: And how would Singapore's AAA credit rating be impacted with the borrowing?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am therefore happy to hear the Deputy Prime Minister's announcement that GST will be extended to cross-border e-commerce transactions of lower value goods, which is expected to grow exponentially in the coming years.

sections.label: Foreign workforce reduction during pandemic
sections.summary: The foreign workforce was reduced by 16% during the pandemic, JSS support was restricted to locals, and border closures disrupted foreign labour supply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The foreign workforce was reduced by 16% during the pandemic, that is, in one year, 16%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: JSS support was restricted to locals and rightfully so, and the closure of borders disrupted the supply of foreign labour.

sections.label: Jobs, training and gig workers
sections.summary: The speaker favours jobs and training over unemployment benefits, wants a faster safety net, and cites the UK Supreme Court ruling on Uber drivers as workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: To keep unemployment low, I think it is right that we focus our efforts on providing jobs and training rather than unemployment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, with greater disruption and uncertainty, it is imperative that we find ways to hasten the safety net for those who are still unable to secure employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For gig workers, we should heed the recent ruling by the UK's Supreme Court, that Uber drivers be considered "workers" and not "independent contractors", entitled to certain protections over their pay and working conditions.

sections.label: Next pandemic and Disease X
sections.summary: COVID-19 is a grave threat, but the next pandemic must be assumed to be much worse, such as a more contagious and deadly Disease X.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: COVID-19 is a grave threat, but we must assume the next pandemic will be much worse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Imagine what researchers call "Disease X", an unknown pathogen more contagious than COVID-19, more deadly than SARS.

sections.label: Going upstream on vaccines
sections.summary: Beyond fill-and-finish vaccine production and regional distribution, Singapore needs to analyse pandemics, develop vaccines and medications, and manufacture them quickly onshore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government has spoken about "fill-and-finish" production and regional distribution for COVID-19 vaccines. "Fill-and-finish" means filling the containers, the vials with vaccine and then finishing the packaging of vaccine for distribution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We can and need to go beyond this and to go upstream.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We need to be able to analyse new pandemics, develop new vaccines and new medications and to manufacture them quickly onshore – quickly, at speed.

sections.label: Singapore developing next pandemic vaccine
sections.summary: Being among the first countries to develop a vaccine for the next pandemic would benefit Singaporeans, the economy and the world, under the published RIE 2025 strategy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If Singapore can be among the first countries to develop a vaccine for the next pandemic, it will be good for our fellow Singaporeans, good for our economy and good for the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have a published strategy for Research, Innovation and Enterprise – RIE 2025.

sections.label: Investing in research for future pandemics
sections.summary: The speaker calls for increased research investment and bolder projects, noting COVID response came from SARS-era biomedical investments and battling Disease X depends on today's actions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chasing challenging mission statements beyond what is capable today but thereby setting goals that can improve human health, improve the environment, improve sustainability and the economy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I call on this Government: increase our investments in research, be even bolder in the projects we choose.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Our ability to respond to COVID was learnt through the hard journey of SARS and the investments in biomedical research more than two decades ago.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Our ability to battle Disease X and survive the next pandemic will depend on what we do today.

sections.label: Recruiting private sector mid-career talent
sections.summary: Candidates who previously would not have considered the public sector should be recruited and retained from mid-career and experienced private sector backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These are candidates who previously because of their journeys would not have considered joining the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We should not squander the opportunity to recruit and retain mid-career and experienced private sector talent from these diverse backgrounds.

sections.label: Support for the Budget
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Budget as it is today and as it can be tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We must be bold enough to make necessary dreams into necessary reality.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so I stand in support of our Budget – what it is today and what it can be tomorrow.

sections.label: Singapore economy recovery projection
sections.summary: The Singapore economy is projected to recover 4% to 6% this year, after a 5.8% contraction in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the Singapore economy is projected to make a recovery of between 4% and 6% this year, this recovery is set against the backdrop of a 5.8% contraction in 2020 and is from a relatively low starting position compared to pre-COVID-19 years.

sections.label: Nurses and healthcare workers' salaries
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Government's plan to enhance salaries of nurses and healthcare workers, calling it long overdue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The recent announcement that the Government will enhance the salary of nurses and healthcare workers is long overdue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nurses and allied healthcare workers have traditionally formed the bulk of all medical workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am thus glad to learn that the Government is planning to enhance the salary of nurses and healthcare workers so that their wages are, perhaps, more commensurate with the work that they do.

sections.label: Progression ladder for enrolled nurses
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will create a progression ladder for enrolled nurses, with training and scholarships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This pathway of progression is generally different for enrolled nurses who typically are those who possess a Nitec in Nursing from the ITE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, while we enhance the salary level for nurses as a whole, I hope the Government will consider putting in place a progression ladder similar to those of registered nurses by taking into consideration their experience on the job, providing them with skills upgrading opportunities through both formal and on-the-job training, and even more scholarships for those who desire to enter the nursing profession and to those who aspire to higher qualifications in the nursing profession.

sections.label: Attractiveness of nursing profession
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will double-down on Future Nursing Career Review Committee recommendations to make nursing more attractive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Perhaps, they are deterred by the long working hours, stress from having to deal manage difficult patients, their family members and expectations, as well as potential disruptions to family life arising from irregular work shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can consider doubling-down on the recommendations made by the Future Nursing Career Review Committee and enhance the attractiveness of the profession for local Singaporeans.

sections.label: Petrol duties and car-lite society
sections.summary: The speaker supports the green agenda but notes petrol duty rises affect those unable to switch transport modes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I agree that in a concerted effort to push Singapore towards a car-lite society and to encourage the use of cleaner fuel and electric vehicles for sustainability, one would find it hard to argue against the rationale for supporting this green agenda.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Now, the immediate rise in petrol duties, however, will no doubt have more of an impact on some groups than others, specifically those who need their vehicles for practical and professional uses, and they are unable to switch over to alternate mode of transportation – be it electric vehicles or other forms of public transport in the short to mid term.

sections.label: Petrol duty rebates for drivers
sections.summary: The rise in petrol duties raises drivers' daily operating costs, and the speaker asks how rebates will reach taxi and private-hire drivers and whether they can be extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Yet, the rise in petrol duties will impact this group significantly, and possibly negating some of the COVID-19 related assistance that they are already receiving elsewhere, as these drivers would have experienced an immediate increase in their daily operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I know that to cushion the impact of the hike in petrol duties, the Government has announced road tax and petrol duty rebates for car owners, taxis and private-hire cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, while the price hikes have been immediate, I believe that the road tax rebates and the duty rebates may come somewhat later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The other point I would like to make, Mr Speaker, Sir, is, that while those who own their cars will receive their rebates directly, how can the Government ensure that taxi companies and car-rental companies pass on the savings to their drivers or hirers in as timely a manner as possible?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Also, will the Government be open to extending the rebates for taxi drivers and private hire car drivers beyond the present period if required?

sections.label: Safeguards against unjustified price rises
sections.summary: The speaker hopes measures helping families are not offset by companies raising prices, and asks the Government to consider safeguards against unjustified fare, fee and price increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I hope that in this particular case, those measures to help these families will not be possibly offset by a rise in prices that some companies might choose to implement, citing the petrol price rises as a possible reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I hope the Government can actually consider putting in safeguards to curb unjustified increases in fares, fees and prices to help protect a wider range of consumers and customers in this regard.

sections.label: Budget 2021 fiscal balance
sections.summary: Budget 2021 must balance using finite fiscal resources to close the output gap against providing fiscal incentives for medium to long-term productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2021 therefore, has to find a balance between using fiscal resources which are finite, to close the output gap; that is, to fight recession on one hand and providing fiscal incentives to spur structural transformation to achieve a medium to long-term productivity growth of say, 2% per annum, on the other hand.

sections.label: Affected sector output and layoffs
sections.summary: The affected sector contracted most during the circuit breaker, and without international tourists and JSS wage subsidies, businesses must cut output and lay off workers.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The affected sector contracted output most obviously during the circuit breaker period, but even post-circuit-breaker, the non-arrival of international tourists means that businesses in the affected sector must cut back output and would have to lay off workers in the absence of wage subsidies given under the Jobs Support Scheme or JSS.

sections.label: Wage subsidies to keep workers
sections.summary: If workers were retrenched, firms would incur new investment and orientation costs, so JSS wage subsidies remain needed to let affected-sector firms keep their workers.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should normal conditions return to the affected sector, firms – if the workers had been retrenched earlier – would have to incur costs once again to make new investment, to orientate new employees.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, there remains a need to provide wage subsidies through the Jobs Support Scheme to enable firms in the affected sector to keep their workers.

sections.label: Scaling down stimulus if pandemic prolonged
sections.summary: If the pandemic is prolonged, efficiency considerations dictate that fiscal stimulus be gradually scaled down despite the argument for keeping businesses afloat.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should the pandemic turn out to be prolonged, then, despite the argument I have just made, that fiscal resources be expended to keep businesses in the affected sector afloat and to avoid retrenchment, the consideration of efficiency dictates that fiscal stimulus be gradually scaled down.

sections.label: Fiscal resources for worker reskilling
sections.summary: An increasing share of fiscal resources should be directed at supporting workers, including those previously employed in the affected sector, to reskill for new job positions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An increasing share of fiscal resources should, therefore, on this principle that I have argued, be directed at supporting workers, including those previously employed in the affected sector, to reskill to fill these new job positions.

sections.label: Contingencies Fund extra $13 billion
sections.summary: The Contingencies Fund, referred to by Deputy Prime Minister Heng in last year's Fortitude Budget, sets aside an extra $13 billion, addressing the concern mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Contingencies Fund, which Deputy Prime Minister Heng referred to in last year's Fortitude Budget, sets aside an extra $13 billion, and that, goes some way to address the concern that I just mentioned.

sections.label: Unemployment insurance scheme trade-offs
sections.summary: Self insurance and a national unemployment insurance scheme are alternatives for cash when a resident is out of work after JSS ceases, but self insurance is not possible for hand-to-mouth workers.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Self insurance and a national unemployment insurance scheme are alternatives for providing the needed cash should a resident be out of work after JSS ceases.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Self insurance, however, is not possible for hand-to-mouth workers.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We, therefore, I believe, need to examine the costs and benefits of providing social insurance to cover the risk of unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As extending unemployment benefits tends – other things being equal – to increase the duration of unemployment as workers are able to hold out longer before taking on a job, there is the prospect that introducing a national unemployment insurance scheme can raise the overall rate of unemployment.

sections.label: Fiscal resources for structural transformation
sections.summary: If the slump is prolonged, fiscal resources should be directed more towards facilitating structural transformation, and there may be a need to study whether a national unemployment insurance scheme is warranted.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If the slump is prolonged, efficiency considerations dictate that fiscal resources should be directed more towards facilitating structural transformation to raise the productive capacity of the economy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There may also be a need to study whether a national unemployment insurance scheme is warranted to provide workers with liquidity in the event of future, future long and deep recessions.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive and SGUnited programmes
sections.summary: The Jobs Growth Incentive aims to help people get jobs in growth sectors by encouraging employers to create and hire early, alongside SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways, Skills, and Traineeship programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Jobs Growth Incentive (JCI) is aimed at helping people get jobs in the growth sectors by encouraging employers to create and hire early for these roles in these sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme which offers company attachments; the SGUnited Skills for mid-career individuals; SGUnited Traineeship Programme for fresh graduates.

sections.label: Graduate employment and part-time work
sections.summary: A Straits Times article reported that employment for fresh graduates from local Universities increased in 2020 from 2019, but part-time or temporary work rose to 22.3% from 7%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It was reported in a recent Straits Times article this month that employment for fresh graduates from our local Universities increased in 2020 from 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, the number that started in part-time or temporary work has increased to 22.3%, up from the 7% the previous year with more than half indicating that they did so because they had no choice.

sections.label: Women in STEM university cohort
sections.summary: Women in STEM made up 41% of the university cohort in 2019, up from 38% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Another point I want to highlight is the topic of skills and talent and the talent pool that women make up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is indeed heartening that the number of women in science, tech, engineering and maths, or STEM as we call it, in our University cohort in 2019 was up to 41%, from 38% in 2017.

sections.label: GST increase and Assurance Package
sections.summary: A $6 billion Assurance Package offsets GST increases, with 60% of net GST borne by foreigners, tourists and top households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But I think that more needs to be done to understand what is it that it is going to take to attract more women to take tech careers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Now, let me touch on the thorny issue of raising GST to finance recurrent spending.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Raising GST will impact Singaporeans, and as announced in last year's Budget, a $6 billion Assurance Package has been set aside to help cushion the impact of the GST increase on Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What this equates to for a majority of Singaporean households is the offsets will cover at least five years' worth of additional expenses incurred because of the higher GST, with more going to the lower income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Those living in 1-room to 3-room HDB flats will receive offsets equivalent to about 10 years of additional GST expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The question is: why raise tax, then give reliefs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I think Deputy Prime Minister Heng also said in his speech was the majority or 60% of the net GST borne by households and individuals is actually borne by foreigners residing in Singapore, tourists and the top 20% of resident households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The question I have is that, with the impact of COVID and the lower number of tourists as well as the impact of COVID-19 on foreigners working and living in Singapore, how does this affect that amount that was projected for the GST increase?

sections.label: Means-testing and COVID business impact
sections.summary: The speaker asks to remove the annual property value criterion for short-term support, citing SBF survey findings on COVID-19 impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For means-testing for application and eligibility for short-term support to assist individuals and families to manage such disruptions, I would like to ask the Minister if consideration can be made to remove the criterion of annual value of the property of the home, for those who own one property or do not own the property they live in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I know this is a tough decision but I hope that some consideration can be made because we have seen the exception was quite large during this period because of the short-term needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the recent national business study conducted by the Singapore Business Federation or SBF, about two-thirds of businesses reported that they were negatively impacted by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And looking ahead, about one-third are unsure about the future of their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And amongst those negatively impacted, 70% thinks that it will take more than a year to fully recover from the pandemic.

sections.label: Vaccination, Resilience Package, Jobs Growth Incentive
sections.summary: The vaccination programme, COVID-19 Resilience Package and Jobs Growth Incentive with SGUnited Jobs and Skills support businesses and local hiring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: With the vaccination programme underway, there is optimism going forward and businesses are encouraged by the COVID-19 Resilience Package that will help safeguard public health and provide targeted help for the hardest hit sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: The additional Jobs Growth Incentive with SGUnited Jobs and Skills to support employers to accelerate hiring of local workers will help businesses and employees move up the value chain together.

sections.label: Manufacturing S Pass ceiling reduction
sections.summary: The Budget 2021 reduction in S Pass Dependency Ratio Ceiling worries manufacturing firms amid expectation mismatches; Budget 2021 has tech, skills, capital and vision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: In the Manufacturing sector, the reduction in S Pass Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) announced in Budget 2021 is worrisome for many of them, especially when Singaporeans may have expectation mismatches and not aspire to those jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: Nett, my view is that the Budget 2021 has the critical elements of tech, plus skills, plus capital, plus vision.

sections.label: Investing in Singaporean tech graduates
sections.summary: One suggestion to address the tech talent crunch is encouraging companies to invest in Singaporean university, polytechnic and ITE graduates for entry-level tech jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: One suggestion specifically to address the tech talent crunch is to encourage our companies to invest in Singaporean graduates, whether University, Polytechnic and ITE graduates for entry-level tech jobs, despite being able to hire experienced foreign developers at equivalent salaries.

sections.label: Workplace fair practice review
sections.summary: The passage states that fair practice in the workplace needs an urgent review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: Fair practice in the workplace needs an urgent review.

sections.label: EDB and skills transfer
sections.summary: The speaker calls the EDB one of the best marketing engines and urges restarting skills and knowledge transfer talks in the board room.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: Our EDB is one of the best marketing engine you can ever find on earth; serious.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: And I would urge that, perhaps, this conversation of skills transfer, knowledge transfer, how many Jessica Tans and how many Russel Thams they are going to develop for us in Singapore, needs to be re-started in the board room – between the Singapore EDB and the MNC head honchos both at HQ and here.

sections.label: SBF Foundation matched TAC funds
sections.summary: SBF Foundation matched funds raised by the TACs, with $1.9 million raised and projected to help over 3,000 employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: SBF Foundation matched the funds raised by the TACs and together, $1.9 million was raised and it is projected to help more than 3,000 employees in those industries.

sections.label: Employability Fund and Empower Circles
sections.summary: SBF Foundation, supported by Tote Board, set up the Employability Fund and Empower Circles to train and re-design work for vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: SBF Foundation, which is the social impact arm of the SBF, with support by Tote Board, has set up the Employability Fund and Empower Circles to work with and rally businesses to train and re-design work for these vulnerable groups, to provide job coach support linkages and so on.

sections.label: Temasek, LLEs and dreams
sections.summary: The passage notes Temasek's $500 million match in Budget 2021 for LLEs and sets out the speaker's dreams for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: Temasek has been a big champion in this movement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: We can see in Budget 2021 where Temasek has come out with a $500 million match by Government to support the LLEs in Singapore to become true local champions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: I have a dream – of a Singapore where a culture of care and dialogue amongst all stakeholders for the common good for all and for the greater good of the economy, our health, the environment and society is part of our DNA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: I have a dream – where citizens, residents, businesses, civil society and Government work together and take an integral development approach to tackle the issues at hand, always ensuring the poorer amongst us, the disadvantaged, the vulnerable families and SMEs are not left behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: I have a dream – that, in Singapore, we have diversity and inclusion in education, digital access, work opportunities, business leadership and politics – at all levels from workers to businesses and society at large; where we practise fair and just code of ethics which reflect our Singapore values; where we guard our racial and religious harmony; and that we, as a people, do not lose our strengths of being a caring and welcoming society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: I have a dream – of a Singapore where our people and organisations are confident to embrace and lead in the innovation, development and application of new technologies and new ideas because we are a learning nation, strong in collaborating with the best minds in the world, and always restlessly re-inventing ourselves to stay humbly relevant in the global economy.

sections.label: Support for the Budget
sections.summary: The speaker concludes by expressing support for the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: With this, I conclude with my support for the Budget.

sections.label: Healthcare worker salary enhancements
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Budget enhancements to salaries of healthcare workers, including nurses and support care workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, I am heartened that the salaries of all our healthcare workers, including both our nurses and our support care workers, will be enhanced under the Budget.

sections.label: Singapore nurse pay comparison
sections.summary: A 2018 Lien Foundation report found Singapore nurses' average monthly pay of S$3,000 was lowest among five Asia Pacific advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The 2018 report by the Lien Foundation showed that, amongst the five advanced economies with ageing populations in the Asia Pacific region, the average monthly pay of nurses was the lowest in Singapore, at S$3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is almost half of the average pay of nurses in Australia, at S$5,780.

sections.label: Petrol duty increases announced
sections.summary: The speaker raises environmental policies from the Budget Statement, specifically immediate duty increases of 15 cents and 10 cents per litre on premium and intermediate petrol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second issue I would like to raise relates to the environmental policies which were announced during the Budget Statement, specifically, the immediate increase in the duties on premium and intermediate petrol by 15 cents and 10 cents per litre respectively.

sections.label: Drivers' estimated cost increase
sections.summary: CNA reported that some drivers estimate their costs will rise by about $60 to $100 a month after the announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Following the announcement, CNA reported that some drivers estimate that their costs will go up by about $60 to $100 a month.

sections.label: Lower-income household income declines
sections.summary: A Beyond Social Services report showed median household income of families seeking help fell from S$1,600 to S$500 monthly, and DOS figures showed a 6.1% real income decline for the bottom 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In early February 2021, Beyond Social Services released a report which showed that the median household income of families who sought help from it fell from S$1,600 to S$500 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Similarly, the Department of Statistics (DOS) released figures showing that the median income of the bottom 10% of lower income households saw a 6.1% decline in real income, compared to 1.4% to 3.2% in other households.

sections.label: Call to review petrol duty hike
sections.summary: The speaker calls the petrol duty increase right but wrongly timed, and echoes Mr Pritam Singh's call for the Government to review the immediate hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, most would agree on the need to take urgent step action in order to address climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the decision to increase the duties on petrol at this time is a case of "doing the right thing but with the wrong timing".

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding all this, Sir, I acknowledge, that the decision has already been made and implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I echo the call made by the Leader of the Opposition, Mr Pritam Singh, for the Government to consider reviewing the immediate hike in the petrol duties rates.

sections.label: Foreign nurses and tudung
sections.summary: The passage notes foreign nurses in healthcare institutions and that some Muslim women forgo nursing because they cannot wear the tudung.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As we know, we have many foreign nurses in our healthcare institutions, especially in the restructured hospitals and polyclinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It cannot be denied that there are some Muslim women who have to forgo their wish to serve as nurses because they know that they will not be allowed to wear the tudung.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the same time, it will also increase the number of local nurses and make nursing in Singapore become more inclusive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In English): Hence, my views and concern on one, nurses' remuneration; two, increase in petrol litre rates; and three, sustainable environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The intent of my sharing is to contribute to our nation's on-going discussions and efforts to bounce from this crisis with greater strength and unity, emerging stronger together.

sections.label: CDC vouchers grant
sections.summary: The Government gave the CDCs an additional $150 million grant, benefiting 1.3 million Singaporean households with $100 CDC Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, let me thank the Government for the additional $150 million grant provided to the CDCs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This will benefit 1.3 million Singaporean households who will receive $100 CDC Vouchers that can be used at participating heartland shops and hawker centres.

sections.label: Green Bonds issuance
sections.summary: The Government will issue Green Bonds for up to $19 billion of identified public sector green projects to deepen market liquidity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To finance this, the Government will issue new bonds, Green Bonds on selected public infrastructures, up to $19 billion of public sector green projects already identified.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The issuance of Green Bonds will deepen market liquidity for Green Bonds attract green issuers, capital, as well as investors, and anchor Singapore as a Green finance hub.

sections.label: EV charging points
sections.summary: The passage notes insufficient charging points for EV users and plans for 28,000 charging points by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have all heard how one of the areas of contention is that there is just not enough charging points for those who opt in for EV at this moment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I note the plans to have 28,000 charging points by 2030 and that commercial entities can be roped in to help build up this infrastructure.

sections.label: Singapore car population 2020
sections.summary: As of 2020, Singapore's car population was about 974,000 according to LTA data.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As of 2020, our car population was about 974,000 – which is near to one million – according to LTA data.

sections.label: Road tax petrol rebates
sections.summary: Motorists will receive road tax and additional petrol duty rebates from 1 August this year to 31 July next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government has announced that motorists would be given road tax and additional petrol duty rebates to help offset the higher costs but all these changes is only applicable from 1 August onwards this year all the way to 31 July next year.

sections.label: COE lifespan for EVs
sections.summary: Asks whether the 10-year COE lifespan can be reviewed and extended for EVs, which pollute less.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With EVs, can we now review this 10-year COE lifespan?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Is it possible for us to consider a longer lifespan for COE for EVs since EVs are less of a pollution, and definitely, frequent changing of cars is not environmentally friendly?

sections.label: Green industry jobs and training
sections.summary: Asks how many green industry jobs the Singapore Green Plan will create and how workforce skill training will be provided.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister also share with us overall how many new jobs can be expected to be created for the green industry in Singapore, under the Singapore Green Plan, when all the EVs plan is being implemented?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How is the Government planning to provide the skill training to our workforce so they can take advantage of this new growth industry?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Over three decades, he took night classes, was loyal, worked hard and got promoted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But in 2003, SARS hit Singapore and many in his rank could not be retained.

sections.label: Businesses worry over wage support
sections.summary: Local businesses worry they may not keep people employed when wage support runs out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among local businesses, there is worry that when wage support runs out, they may not be able to keep people employed.

sections.label: Graduate employment survey findings
sections.summary: The annual Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey found 69.8% of fresh graduates in permanent full-time jobs, down from 81.7%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The annual Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey last year found that 69.8% of fresh graduates from permanent full-time jobs down from 81.7% the year before.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills incentives
sections.summary: The SGUnited Jobs and Skills package gives firms incentives to employ mature local hires above 40, persons with disabilities and ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package, there is some incentive for firms who employ mature local hires above 40 years old, persons with disabilities and ex-offenders.

sections.label: Blue Plan marine environment recommendations
sections.summary: In 2018, more than 100 people contributed to the third edition of the Blue Plan, which has six recommendations on protecting the marine environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is a chance for us to approach recovery the right way – to ensure that it is not growth at all costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But did you know that in 2018, more than 100 people contributed to the third edition of the Blue Plan, which has six recommendations in protecting our marine environment?

sections.label: EV adoption chasm
sections.summary: EVs are 0.2% of cars, and Geoffrey Moore says adoption must cross a 15% to 18% chasm for widespread adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on reports, the number of EVs on the road makes up 0.2% of the cars in circulation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Geoffrey Moore, who studies patterns of adoption suggests that there is a chasm of adoption between the early market and the mainstream market that sits between 15% and 18% of adoption rates and crossing that chasm will see widespread adoption, while failing to cross that chasm will see these technologies fail to make it to mainstream.

sections.label: EV incentives and charging concerns
sections.summary: Many incentives stop by 2023, possibly before the chasm is crossed, and charging access is a top consumer concern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many of the incentives have a stop date by 2023 attached to them and it may take us longer than that to cross the chasm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the biggest consumer concerns when it comes to EVs is reliable, convenient and consistent access to charging stations or better yet, supercharging stations.

sections.label: M3 support for vulnerable groups
sections.summary: She worked in a warehouse as a pest fumigator, and M3 efforts like FITRAH and Ciptasama should include at-risk youths and offenders' families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: When she came out, she worked in a warehouse as a pest fumigator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that efforts, through the M3 framework, such as FITRAH, Ciptasama and youth mentoring will be resourced, evolved and diversified to include particularly vulnerable groups, such as at-risk youths, and spouses and children of repeat offenders who may be stuck in cycles of not having hope, on a structural and consistent basis working in partnership with Malay/Muslim organisations, many of which are looking forward and are grateful for the announcement on support for charity sector.

sections.label: Five Budgets support
sections.summary: Five Budgets totalling around $100 billion last year supported businesses and Singaporeans through a difficult period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The unprecedented series of five Budgets, totalling around $100 billion last year, were pivotal in supporting our businesses and Singaporeans through this difficult period.

sections.label: SME credit and guarantees
sections.summary: Personal guarantees disadvantage smaller businesses, so credit initiatives need calibration for SMEs at specific growth stages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Here is one example: one condition to get credit often involves providing personal guarantees by the entrepreneur, despite risk-sharing by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This puts smaller businesses at a disadvantage and those who really need help may not get the help needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, the initiatives to provide more credit and financing needs to be calibrated and fine-tuned for SMEs who are in a specific stage of growth.

sections.label: Hawkerpreneur support measures
sections.summary: Measures for smaller businesses like hawker stalls need to be specific and bespoke so hawkerpreneurs provide affordable food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We want our hawkerpreneurs to do well, and continue to provide affordable and diverse food options for our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, our measures for smaller businesses like hawker stalls needs to be specific and bespoke.

sections.label: Business consultancy with training
sections.summary: Business consultancy should go hand-in-hand with training so that training for all staff levels matches the business growth stage and journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Crucially, business consultancy should go hand-in-hand with training so that training for all level of staff within a business is tailored to match the business growth stage and journey.

sections.label: Green adoption and Singapore Green Plan
sections.summary: DPM Heng's Budget initiatives to catalyse green adoption provide a green beacon, and the Singapore Green Plan is an economic growth opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng's Budget initiatives to catalyse green adoption provides the necessary green beacon for us to rally on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe the Singapore Green Plan is an economic growth opportunity and positions our economy and businesses favourably as more investors and end consumers are demanding more from the products and businesses, based on their overall impact to the environment and society.

sections.label: Impact investments and ESG for businesses
sections.summary: With growing wealth management and family offices keen on impact investments, local businesses, especially SMEs, need help to embrace the ESG mandate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With a growing wealth management base in Singapore and more investors, especially family offices, keen on impact investments where investments achieve both economic gains and social impact, we need to position our entrepreneurs to ride this wave of new investors and end consumers consciousness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By assisting our local businesses to re-position their business models ensures: one, that our local businesses tap on the growing appetite of impact investments thereby creating opportunities for wealth managed to flow into our local economy; two, build greater resilience, greater resilience, as more clients and end consumers are shifting their purchasing preferences to value for money and value for good; and three, expands both economic value and deep societal value of an enterprise, transforming businesses into agents of societal change, that value adds to our society and improves our societal well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We really need to help as many businesses, especially SMEs to embrace the ESG mandate.

sections.label: Crisis opportunities and K-shape recovery
sections.summary: The current crisis presents opportunities for growth, but boldly seizing them will augment the K-shape economic recovery already seen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current crisis is presenting us now with opportunities for growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, boldly seizing these opportunities will augment the K-shape economic recovery we are already seeing.

sections.label: Revitalising economy and sustainable development pillars
sections.summary: After two years of dipping into past reserves, revitalising and growing the economy is paramount, while sustainable development has social, environmental and economic pillars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After two consecutive years of dipping into our past reserves and being in a still highly uncertain economic situation, revitalising and growing the economy now is paramount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am very glad we are now giving climate change and social equity more emphasis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But we also have to remember, sustainable development has three key pillars: social, environmental and economic.

sections.label: Island with limited resources and land
sections.summary: Singapore is an island with limited resources and a little more than 700 sq km of land for a city, country and nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: No matter how sick we are of hearing this, it will always be true that we are an island with limited resources and a little more than 700 sq km of land to accommodate the needs of a city, country and nation.

sections.label: Regulator and promoter role
sections.summary: Private companies with long-term growth plans want Singapore to succeed, and the speaker applauds ministries acting as both regulator and promoter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should bear in mind that private companies that have a long-term growth plan in Singapore, also want Singapore to be successful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I applaud the Ministries and agencies that have the wisdom to take on the twin role of regulator and promoter for the sectors they are in charge of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even as they regulate the sector for "common good", they also promote the sector’s growth and innovation.

sections.label: ESG in business decisions
sections.summary: A clear trend exists among global corporates and investors to factor ESG considerations more into business decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, there is already a clear trend among global corporates and investors that ESG – Environmental, Social and Governance –considerations are being factored more in their business decisions.

sections.label: Open Innovation Platform proposal
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Open Innovation Platform and proposes opening it to the Pro-Enterprise Panel with funding and access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As such, I am heartened to hear the Deputy Prime Minister announce the Open Innovation Platform, which facilitates the matching of problems faced by companies and public agencies, with solution providers from the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: To accelerate this process, I would like to further propose that the Open Innovation Platform be opened up to the Pro-Enterprise Panel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Many of these complexities can only be described as "wicked" problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Now, if the Pro-Enterprise Panel is given the funding and access to the Open Innovation Platform, I strongly believe we can come up with even better and faster solutions to cut red tape while ensuring governance.

sections.label: Upgrading sub-industry TACs
sections.summary: The Government should upgrade sub-industry TACs, second officials, and if needed create a parallel TAC with established players.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As such, I believe the Government should go big to upgrade various sub-industry TACs, including seconding capable industry officials there, and help them strengthen their relationship with the businesses they serve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And if for some reasons, these sub-industry TACs are not forthcoming to change, I sincerely hope the Government can proactively work with the established players to create a parallel TAC, one that can move the sub-industry forward.

sections.label: Policies for senior workers
sections.summary: Forward-looking policies for senior workers already exist, such as the Special Employment Credit and the Retirement and Re-employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Today, we already have forward-looking policies for our senior workers, such as the Special Employment Credit or the Retirement and Re-employment Act.

sections.label: Gig economy for seniors
sections.summary: The Government can create a gig economy for seniors through micro-jobs, a national digital platform and app, and SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Our Government can take the lead to create a gig economy for our seniors by doing three things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One, creating micro-jobs for our seniors starting with those in social services sectors; two, creating a national digital platform and app; and, three, equipping our seniors to do micro-jobs through SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Hiring one nurse versus senior helper
sections.summary: The passage asks why staffing is not reduced to one nurse while hiring a trained senior living nearby to carry patients and assist with wound dressing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Why do we not cut it down to one nurse instead and hire a trained senior living, perhaps, in a nearby block or street, to provide the necessary support, such as carrying the patients and assisting in wound dressing?

sections.label: Certifying grandmothers and retired teachers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether able grandmothers could be certified for infant care and retired teachers for after-school care in their own homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can we certify some of our able grandmothers to provide infant care services for a few infants in their homes, or retired teachers to provide after school care for a few students at their own home?

sections.label: COVID-19 Budget measures impact estimates
sections.summary: The passage states the Government committed nearly $100 billion in COVID-19 packages, and MAS estimated the five 2020 Budgets supported GDP growth by 5.5%, about $28 billion, saving or creating 155,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last year, the Government committed nearly $100 billion through various packages to support Singaporeans and the economy through the COVID-19 crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a report released by MOF on the impact of the COVID-19 Budget measures, it was stated that MAS estimated that the five Budgets in 2020 supported GDP growth by 5.5% in 2020, representing only about $28 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MAS also estimated that the measures saved or created 155,000 jobs.

sections.label: Measuring measures and $900 million allocation
sections.summary: The passage says measuring each measure's effectiveness aids future allocations, and states the latest $900 million for Singapore households is inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Measuring the effectiveness of each measure will help us make better allocations in future – like should more transfers go to companies or to families and individuals in need?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe that the latest $900 million allocated to help Singapore households ride out the COVID-19 crisis is inadequate.

sections.label: Wage share of GDP target
sections.summary: The passage compares Singapore's 2020 wage share of GDP of about 43.6% with Germany's 54% and the UK's 53%, and proposes a target of at least 50%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to SingStats, in 2020, wages formed about 43.6% of GDP while operating surplus of corporates and other organisations formed about 56.2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In comparison, according to OECD Statistics, the German wage component of GDP was 54% while operating surplus was 37%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, in the UK, the wage component was 53% of GDP and the operating surplus, 39%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If we want to ensure that our people enjoy the benefits of this economic growth, we should set an initial target of having the wage component form at least 50% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This should be an important KPI for the Government moving forward.

sections.label: Slowing GDP growth and firm losses
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's five-year average GDP growth through 2019 was 2.9% versus global 3.4%, return on equity fell to a 20-year low of 5.9%, and 35% of listed firms were loss making in Q4 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even prior to 2020, our five-year average GDP growth rate through 2019 is at 2.9%, lagging that of the global economy at 3.4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If we use the public markets as a proxy to the state of corporate performance in Singapore, return on equity for the Singapore market, ex-financials, has also seen a steady decline, falling to a 20-year low of 5.9% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the fourth quarter of 2019, 35% of firms listed in Singapore were already loss making, the highest since the 2008-2009 Global Financial Crisis.

sections.label: SMEs share of GDP
sections.summary: SMEs are 99% of companies and employ 72% of the workforce, but their GDP contribution fell from 50% in 2014 to 44% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, SMEs represent 99% of companies in Singapore and employ 72% of our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, SMEs contribute just 44% to Singapore's GDP in 2019, having steadily declined from 50% in 2014.

sections.label: Budget deficit and surplus figures
sections.summary: The Government expects an $11.0 billion deficit, or 2.2% of GDP, while receipts less expenditure from 2011 to 2020 would total about $205 billion surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government expects an overall budget deficit of $11.0 billion, or 2.2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Had we taken the total estimated receipts of $103.7 billion, less the total expenditure of $107.2 billion, then the deficit would have been a more modest $3.5 billion or 0.7% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If we extend this analysis and took the total receipts less the total expenditure over the last 10 years from 2011 to 2020, then the total surplus would have amounted to about $205 billion.

sections.label: NIRC contributions rising
sections.summary: NIRC contributions are expected to rise from $17 billion in 2019 to $18.1 billion in 2020 and $19.5 billion in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Further, I observe that in the official Budget, NIRC contributions are expected to continue its steady path of increase, from $17 billion in 2019 to $18.1 billion in 2020 and $19.5 billion in 2021.

sections.label: Members meeting Basic Retirement Sum
sections.summary: The proportion of active members turning 55 who set aside the BRS rose from 62% in 2018 to 66% in 2020, but a third could not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the proportion of active members turning 55 who have been able to set aside the BRS improved from 62% in 2018 to 66% in 2020, there remains a third of active members today who were not even able to have $93,000 in their Retirement Accounts last year.

sections.label: Seniors lacking retirement funds
sections.summary: More than half of seniors do not appear to have sufficient funds to have the option to retire comfortably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Despite a lifetime of hard work and contribution to our nation, sadly more than half of our seniors do not appear to have sufficient funds to have the option to retire comfortably.

sections.label: CPF top-ups and younger generation
sections.summary: CPF top-up efforts may pass the problem to the younger generation, who worry about both their own and their parents' retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And I do recognise efforts by CPF to make it easier for members to top up their own or their loved ones' CPF accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, this only seem to pass the problem to the younger generation, where they not only have to worry about having adequate CPF balances for their retirement, but they also worry for their parents' retirement as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What can we do to ensure that we progress closer to the 100% mark that all Singaporeans are adequately prepared for retirement, with minimal financial stress on the younger generation?

sections.label: Social safety net vulnerability
sections.summary: The pandemic exposed society's vulnerability and the social safety net's inadequacies, and a strong safety net is needed for Singaporeans to face post-COVID challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The pandemic has highlighted the vulnerability of our society and reflected the many inadequacies of our social safety net.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To encourage Singaporeans to face changes more bravely, to transform and accept re-training with more adaptability in the post-COVID era, we need a strong safety net to enable Singaporeans to face future challenges with greater confidence and ease.

sections.label: Sports industry recovery support
sections.summary: The sports industry has not fully recovered, big box gyms were hardest hit, and the Sports Resilience Package will be extended in FY2021 with $45 million added.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, while the industry has partially resumed operations, albeit under strict social distancing controls, the industry has yet to really recover.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are an estimated 500 to 600 sports and fitness establishments in Singapore, serving over 500,000 members and participants through their programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some establishments have recovered better than others, with big box gyms having been the hardest hit, with revenues up to 40% to 50% of the pre-COVID-19 level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Now that Singapore is easing into Phase Three, it is time to focus on the industry and rehabilitation efforts and how we can allow the sports industry, both sports enterprises and people participating in sports, to get back on their feet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am heartened to hear that the Sports Resilience Package will be extended in FY2021 to support businesses and self-employed persons in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am also encouraged to note that an additional $45 million will be set aside for the Arts, Culture and Sports sectors to supply capacity building and sector transformation.

sections.label: Team Singapore Alumni programme
sections.summary: The passage suggests setting up a Team Singapore Alumni programme to recognise Pioneers' accomplishments and let retired athletes contribute to the sporting eco-system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps, it is time to set up a Team Singapore Alumni programme that recognises the accomplishments of our Pioneers and allows retired athletes to continue contributing to the sporting eco-system.

sections.label: E-sports revenue and gaming firms
sections.summary: E-sports revenues in 2020 are expected to grow US$1.1 billion, and gaming firms such as Tencent, Garena, Ubisoft and DEA are locating regional headquarters in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
