sentences.text: E-sports' revenues in 2020 are expected to grow US$1.1 billion, a 15.7% year-on-year growth from 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some of the biggest gaming firms, such as Tencent, Garena, Ubisoft and DEA are locating their regional headquarters in Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore hosting international events
sections.summary: Singapore hosted the Mobile Legends M2 World Championships and the ATP 250 tennis tournament, and organisers are considering hosting events here due to stable conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In January, Singapore played host to the Mobile Legends: Bang Bang M2 World Championships; this week, Singapore hosts the ATP 250 tennis tournament, and other major international events that are on the horizon, such as the World Economic Forum in August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's stable and secure conditions make us an attractive destination to host events in the current global environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Organisers that would not have thought Singapore previously are considering hosting their events here.

sections.label: Heng's $24 billion commitment
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng has committed $24 billion over three years to enable firms and workers to emerge stronger from the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng has committed $24 billion over three years to enable our firms and workers to emerge stronger from this crisis.

sections.label: Venture Debt risk sharing
sections.summary: Government shares up to 70% of risk on eligible Venture Debt loans and raises the loan quantum cap from $5 million to $8 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For the Venture Debt programme, the Government shares up to 70% of the risk on eligible loans with Participating Financial Institutions and even increases the cap on loan quantum supported, from $5 million to $8 million.

sections.label: ComLink expansion nationwide
sections.summary: ComLink will expand from 1,000 families to a nationwide programme benefiting 14,000 families over two years, coordinated with UPLIFT and KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They have been hard hit by the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am delighted that the Community Link (ComLink) initiative will be expanded from 1,000 families to a nationwide programme to benefit 14,000 families over the next two years, in coordination with other schemes such as UPLIFT and KidSTART.

sections.label: Student Care Centre places
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will guarantee students from vulnerable families places in their own schools' Student Care Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For students from vulnerable families, will the Ministry guarantee them places in their own schools' Student Care Centres?

sections.label: Poor diets and child development
sections.summary: An MOE-funded study found children from poorer homes have less healthy diets and food insecurity, linked to health, development and behavioural impacts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As the recent Singapore Longitudinal Early Development Study funded by MOE had found, children from poorer homes have less healthy diets and suffer from food insecurity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Not only do their diets affect their health and development, poor nutrition is linked to, I quote, "aggression, delinquency, anxiety and depression".

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Longer term impact from poor diets in the young includes potential obesity and weaker academic performance.

sections.label: Student Care Fee Assistance coverage
sections.summary: MSF increased subsidies and broadened income criteria for Student Care Fee Assistance since July last year, and the question asks how many more families are covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Since July last year, MSF had increased the subsidies and broaden the income criteria so that more families qualify for the Student Care Fee Assistance scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With these changes, how many more families does the scheme cover?

sections.label: Expansionary Budget size
sections.summary: The Budget provides less support than the prior year but is expansionary at $102 billion, an 8.8% year-over-year increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Although this Budget will not provide as much in support schemes compared to the prior year, I applaud the Government for putting forward an expansionary Budget at $102 billion, representing an 8.8% increase year over year.

sections.label: CSA phishing identification findings
sections.summary: CSA reported in August 2020 that only 6% of people aware of phishing correctly identified all tested phishing emails.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Cyber Security Agency of Singapore, or CSA, too, had similar findings, reporting in August 2020 that, of the people who know about phishing, only 6% in the survey were able to correctly identify all the phishing emails that were tested.

sections.label: Scam cases and elderly victim
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported scam cases grew 65% in 2020, with over $201 million lost, and an 80-year-old resident lost over $400,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On 9 February this year, the Straits Times reported that scam cases grew 65% in 2020 over the prior year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is a record number where more than $201 million were lost across the top 10 scam types.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This topic strikes close to my heart as, in my resident’s case, it left him, an 80-year-old, in a despondent state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: He lost over $400,000, most of this from his retirement savings from the sale of his 5-room flat.

sections.label: Shared burden in digital system
sections.summary: Digital hand-offs create complexity, and consumers and companies must share the burden of protecting the system alongside Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, the interaction of so many digital hand-offs creates complexity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I believe that while the Government is taking the lead, consumers wanting the convenience as well as companies seeking to profit in the digital economy must also bear a fair share of the burden in protecting the system.

sections.label: Recovery, resourcing and fraud standards
sections.summary: The speaker proposes prioritising recovery, national response times, reviewing agency resourcing, developing fraud standards, and cross-jurisdictional cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we need to prioritise recovery so that we have a higher chance to get the funds back, target a national level response time for recovery of domestic fund flows and push for commitments across Government agencies and the private sector to act within the response times agreed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three, with the target response times in mind, review whether our law enforcement and similar agencies are sufficiently resourced and fit for purpose, supported by effective regulations since digital crimes are very different from physical crimes due to anonymity and speed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Four, relevant agencies should develop fraud prevention and detection standards with relevant private sector groups that they interact with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given the knowledge of these criminal typologies, could MHA take the lead as the overall coordinator?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And lastly, there is also a need to increase cross jurisdictional cooperation to come up with a more comprehensive plan to recover funds as more monies are being lost overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I am heartened that this Government has shown commitment and leadership in putting forward an expansionary Budget to put more effort to help Singapore stay ahead and securing Singapore with the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These are truly challenging times as our economy shrank by 5.8%, the worst recession since Independence.

sections.label: Immediate pandemic support schemes
sections.summary: The COVID-19 Recovery Grant, $900 million household support package and JSS sector-specific support provide respite for those most affected by the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For immediate needs, schemes like the COVID-19 Recovery Grant, the $900 million household support package and JSS sector-specific support will be a much-needed respite for those most affected by the pandemic.

sections.label: Post-pandemic digitalisation pilot trap
sections.summary: A McKinsey report indicated 85% of ASEAN companies are still stuck in the digitalisation pilot trap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Only then can we be fully poised to take full advantage of the opportunities emerging from the post-pandemic world economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is noteworthy that a recent McKinsey report indicated that 85% of ASEAN companies are still stuck in this digitalisation pilot trap.

sections.label: Training investment spending plans
sections.summary: The plan is to spend $5.4 billion on training, in addition to $3 billion already spent on the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For investment in training, we plan to spend $5.4 billion in addition to the $3 billion already spent on SGUnited Jobs and Skills package for our workers.

sections.label: Lean sigma course certification example
sections.summary: A lean sigma course participant receives certification only after showing $1 million operational improvement to his organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: An example is the lean sigma course where a participant receives his certification only after showing $1 million operational improvement to his organisation.

sections.label: Budget deficit and family support
sections.summary: This year's Budget is in deficit, aiming to help families and signal economic transformation, with $900 million for the Family Support Package and support for aviation and aerospace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   This year's Budget is in the deficit as it not only aims to help families overcome the pandemic, but also to send a signal about the importance of economic transformation and supporting future growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am confident that the $900 million allocated through the Family Support Package, where low-income families are given more support, will help many families overcome this pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition, specific support for the worst affected sectors, such as the Jobs Support Scheme or JSS, for the aviation and aerospace industries, is very important as it ensures that we retain the talent and workforce available in this strategic sector, while preparing them for the future.

sections.label: Oil prices and driver relief
sections.summary: The 2021 Budget mitigates oil price increases with road tax subsidies, and the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund gives taxi and private rental car drivers $600 monthly from January to March and $450 from April to June.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The increase in oil prices may cause our cost of living to rise, especially for those who use transport to earn a living, but I am heartened that the 2021 Budget mitigates the impact of this price increase with road tax subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund also assists taxi drivers and private rental car drivers who receive $600 per month between January and March and a further $450 between April and June.

sections.label: Local workers duties anywhere
sections.summary: Many local workers, including 60% of PMETs, can perform their duties anywhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In fact, many local workers, including 60% of PMETs, can perform their duties anywhere.

sections.label: Fuel economy workers shift
sections.summary: Workers in the fuel economy need to shift to growth industries, with care to avoid wrong moves, especially low-wage workers, to seize green economy opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Traditional jobs in the fuel economy is more likely to diminish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our workers who are involved in this industry need to shift to industries that show growth potential and we need to manage this process carefully, so that no workers will make the wrong move and get left out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is especially important because, usually, low-wage workers in the industry are also the most vulnerable to structural changes in the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We need to start this process now, so that we are able to take advantage and seize the opportunities available in the new green economy.

sections.label: Budget support and GST assurances
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Budget, citing the $6 billion Assurance Package and GST buffering for lower and middle income groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In English): In summary, Mr Speaker, Sir, I have touched on three suggestions that we need to work on to seize the opportunity as we head towards an inclusive transformation for Singapore’s future: firstly, how do we increase the momentum of real sustainable transformation in digitalisation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: That being said, Mr Speaker, Sir, notwithstanding the arguments above, I stand in support of the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government redistributes taxes, revenues through a progressive system of tax and transfers and one such example is the $6 billion Assurance Package that was announced at the Unity Budget last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: No matter when GST is implemented, the lower and middle income groups will be buffered for 10 and five years respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, additional assurances were also made that when GST is increased on healthcare and education, these increases will be absorbed by the Government.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme extension
sections.summary: The extension of the Jobs Support Scheme is targeted to support workers and businesses and prepare them for a post-pandemic future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The extension of the Jobs Support Scheme is well targeted to support our workers and businesses in this time of need and prepare them for a post pandemic future.

sections.label: SGUnited Skills and Jobs package
sections.summary: SGUnited Skills and the Jobs and Skills package ensure human capital stays agile to changes and growing capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: SGUnited Skills as well as the Jobs and Skills package ensures that our human capital will continue to be agile to changes and growing capabilities.

sections.label: Internet and AI value growth
sections.summary: The Internet created over $13 trillion in value while AI created $2 trillion in 2020, with AI growth expected to surpass the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Over the last two decades, the Internet has created over $13 trillion in value whilst AI has created $2 trillion in just 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The growth in the value of AI is expected to grow at close to 20% CAGR to surpass the value of the Internet by the next decade.

sections.label: AI as general-purpose technology
sections.summary: AI is a general-purpose technology with cross-domain capability to raise all sectors and industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Unlike other sectorial, incremental innovations and creative ideas, unlike existing platforms and eco-systems, AI is a general-purpose technology that has the cross-domain capability to raise all sectors and all industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: It can be the tide that rises all boats.

sections.label: Budget support and SGUnited extension
sections.summary: Quoting HG Wells, the speaker supports the Budget and notes the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package extension will support hiring 200,000 locals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the words of HG Wells in his book "A Short History of the World", written in 1922: "Adapt or perish, now as ever, is nature’s inexorable imperative." Mr Speaker, Sir, I support the Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The extension of SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package will continue to support the hiring of 200,000 locals this year and provide up to 35,000 traineeships and training positions.

sections.label: Scoot flight capacity cut
sections.summary: At the crisis peak, Scoot's parent Singapore Airlines cut 96% of its flight capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: At the height of the crisis, Scoot’s parent company, Singapore Airlines, had to cut 96% of its flight capacity.

sections.label: Scoot crew matched to manufacturing
sections.summary: Scoot Staff Union and UWEEI worked with NTUC's Job Security Council and tripartite partners to match about 300 Scoot flight crew to manufacturing jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Scoot Staff Union together with another Union, the United Workers of Electronics & Electrical Industries (UWEEI) worked closely with NTUC's Job Security Council and our tripartite partners to match some 300 flight crew members from Scoot to jobs in the manufacturing sector.

sections.label: Nurses' pay and essential workers
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Budget announcement enhancing nurses' and support care staff salaries, noting many other essential workers are in the bottom 20 percent of wage earners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As a doctor, as a political officeholder in MOH and as a unionist, I certainly welcome Deputy Prime Minister Heng's announcement in this Budget that the salary of nurses and support care staff will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, many of our other essential workers have incomes at the bottom 20 percent of all wage earners.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model wage growth
sections.summary: 80,000 workers in cleaning, security and landscaping saw about 30% cumulative wage growth over five years, and lift and escalator workers get mandated increases in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Since then, through the combined efforts of the tripartite partners, 80,000 workers in the three mandatory PWM sectors of cleaning, security and landscaping have seen cumulative wage growth of around 30%, compared to 24% for workers at the 20th percentile of wages over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Lift and escalator workers will also soon enjoy mandated annual wage increases in 2022 in the fourth PWM that will become mandatory.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: First, include in-house cleaners and security officers in mandatory PWM.

sections.label: P20/P50 wage ratio comparison
sections.summary: The P20/P50 ratio is about 0.54, while 75% of OECD countries have a ratio of 0.67 or better.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Today, the P20/P50 ratio is about 0.54, indicating that the P20 salary is only about half that of the median income earner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: But 75% of OECD countries have a P20/P50 ratio of 0.67 or better, indicating that the P20 salary is at least two-thirds of the median income earners in these countries, suggesting a narrower wage gap.

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme extended
sections.summary: The Wage Credit Scheme has been extended in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Wage Credit Scheme has been extended in this Budget.

sections.label: Lift technicians PWM wages
sections.summary: After a three-year transition, lift technicians become the fourth group under the mandatory PWM, with over 2,000 benefiting from higher salaries in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Following a three-year transition period, lift technicians will be the fourth group of workers to come under the mandatory PWM and enjoy higher salaries in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Over 2,000 lift technicians in this sector will benefit from a more structured career progression and an uplift to their wages.

sections.label: Food service retail PWM workers
sections.summary: PWMs in the food service and retail sectors will benefit a potential pool of about 70,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: PWMs in food service and retail sectors will benefit a potential pool of about 70,000 workers.

sections.label: NTUC PWM sector discussions
sections.summary: NTUC will begin discussions with relevant sector agencies on key milestones this year to implement a PWM potentially benefiting up to 3,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: NTUC will begin discussions with the relevant sector agencies on the key milestones for this year to implement a PWM in the sector, which could potentially benefit up to 3,000 workers.

sections.label: CTCs and OTR companies
sections.summary: More than 600 CTCs have been formed, over 100 companies embarked on the OTR, and close to 60 did so virtually or hybrid.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To date, more than 600 CTCs have been formed with over 100 companies having already embarked on the OTR.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Close to 60 companies undertook the OTR via a virtual or hybrid approach and we expect more to do so in the months ahead.

sections.label: Waste Management sector OTR PWM
sections.summary: Seventeen Waste Management companies developed a sector OTR in October 2020, spurring a PWM last month uplifting 3,000 local workers' wages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Seventeen companies in the Waste Management Sector came together and developed a sector OTR in October 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Importantly, this sector OTR provided further impetus for the implementation of a PWM for the Waste Management sector last month, uplifting wages of 3,000 local workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In the next two years, NTUC Training and Transformation Group will reach out to more TACs and business groups to pursue Sector OTRs, including sectors like Food Services and Retail where there is a growing consensus to implement PWMs.

sections.label: GST assurance package wealth taxes
sections.summary: The $6 billion assurance package offsets the GST increase for families up to five to 10 years, but higher GST will still hit them thereafter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Just a short clarification on Member Shawn Huang's clarification earlier just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I do recognise that the $6 billion assurance package does go some way to offset the GST increase for families up to between five and 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: But I think, thereafter, the reality of the higher GST will still hit them for the rest of their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: As what another Member, Ms Foo also said, perhaps we could look at wealth taxes being another option if we really do determine that a raise in tax in necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: But I think the broader point that I was raising in my speech is actually is the imposition of such a tax necessary in the first place, especially amidst the macro economic uncertainties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: I do not debate with him on the timeline, on the implementation, but just to say that in Singapore, we need to see the entire tax and benefit system as a holistic system, and that in itself, GST, yes, it is a regressive tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: But when you look at the entire system, it is progressive because of the way it is redistributed.

sections.label: Higher WIS for essential workers
sections.summary: The speaker calls for higher Workfare Income Supplement payouts for essential services workers to acknowledge their social value and hardship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Workfare Income Supplement or WIS has been a welcomed step, but I would like to once again call for the Government to consider providing a higher WIS payout to workers in the essential services to acknowledge their social value and the hardship faced in their line of work.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Models uplift workers
sections.summary: Progressive Wage Models have uplifted around 80,000 workers in Cleaning, Landscape Maintenance and Security, and adequate support benefits all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: By providing adequate support to our workers, all of us will benefit from a more knowledgeable and professional workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have seen and heard how the Progressive Wage Models or PWMs have proved successful in uplifting around 80,000 workers in the Cleaning, Landscape Maintenance and Security sectors with its holistic approach.

sections.label: Wages for PWM sectors and nurses
sections.summary: The speaker says PWM sector wages must match skills and essential services, and applauds enhanced wages for nurses and healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Despite this, we must acknowledge that the wages in these PWM sectors need to commiserate with the skills and the essential services provided by our workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I applaud the announcement made by our Deputy Prime Minister recently to enhance the wages of our nurses and other healthcare workers such as the support care staff.

sections.label: PWM expanded to Waste Management
sections.summary: The PWM was expanded to Waste Management after NTUC lobbying, recognising around 3,000 workers, with the speaker chairing the Tripartite Cluster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Just last month, it was announced that the PWM has been expanded to the Waste Management sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: NTUC had lobbied hard for the expansion into this sector and had engaged the associations and the relevant Government bodies to make this happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is an important step in recognising the efforts of around 3,000 unsung heroes and as the Chair of the Tripartite Cluster for Waste Management, I look forward to continuing with stakeholders to deliberate a PWM for this sector.

sections.label: Facilities Management industry development
sections.summary: A tripartite committee was formed in 2019, a Skills Framework launched, and FMC Accreditation is underway to raise industry competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Facilities Management Implementation Committee was formed, comprising tripartite representatives to develop and implement strategies to create a more dynamic and professional industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Facilities Management Skills Framework was launched in September of last year to provide the industry with information on the occupations, skills and competencies, and the possible career pathways available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The development of an FMC Accreditation is also underway, which will encourage higher management competencies and skillsets for workers in the industry.

sections.label: Foreign Employee Dormitories Act coverage
sections.summary: FEDA regulates foreign worker accommodations for health and safety, but applies only to dormitories housing 1,000 or more workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Foreign Employee Dormitories Act or FEDA ensures that the accommodations of our foreign workers are regulated and must comply with a list of requirements to ensure the health and safety of their residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: However, FEDA only applies to larger dormitories that accommodate 1,000 or more workers.

sections.label: S Pass salary payment rules
sections.summary: Employers of S Pass holders must pay salaries electronically within three months of pass issue and keep payment records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Employers of S Pass holders, for example, are required to pay salaries electronically, start the electronic payments within three months of the issue of the S Pass and maintain a record of salary payments.

sections.label: Calls on WIS, PWM, workers
sections.summary: The speaker calls for higher WIS for essential workers, PWM wage increases, training, rest areas, and review of FEDA coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have worked even harder for them during the COVID-19 pandemic and we will continue working to overcome this crisis together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I have called for: (a) The Government to consider providing a higher WIS payout to workers in the essential services to acknowledge their social value and the hardship faced in their line of work (b) I have called on Service Buyers and Service Providers to provide ample opportunities for their workers to undergo training in order to enhance their skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As for the PWM, I would like to call upon all stakeholders to consider the value of the jobs and increase the PWM wages so that the lives of all Singaporean workers are uplifted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I would also like to call on the Government to consider transitional support to help service buyers as we adjust workers’ wages to commensurate with the value of their work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I have also asked for the PWM to be expanded to other sectors like the pest management and strata management sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In terms of workers’ welfare, I would like to encourage service buyers to set up rest areas for their workers in accordance with the Tripartite Advisory on Provision of Rest Areas for Outsourced Workers, and would also like to take this opportunity to call on the Government to issue a Gross Floor Area waiver for areas stipulated as rest areas to encourage more buildings to set up rest areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I also spoke about migrant workers and would like to call upon the Government to consider a review of FEDA and increase the scope to dormitories that house lesser than 1,000 workers, to ensure that more or all the foreign workers in Singapore will be housed in accommodations that are regulated and meet the minimal provisions for their health and safety.

sections.label: Questions on PWM workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks how many workers will still earn under $1,300, whether self-employed and daily-rated workers will be included, and the rollout timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have a clarification for Senior Minister of State Koh based on his speech just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe Senior Minister of State Koh mentioned in October last year that after implementing the PWM for the cleaning, security and landscaping sectors, there will be a residual 100,000 workers who are still earning less than $1,300 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With the new six sectors added to the PWM fold, how many workers will still be earning less than $1,300 a month?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And are there any plans to include self-employed and daily-rated workers under the PWM?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And lastly, what is the timeline for the rollout of the PWM to these six new sectors plus the vocational PWM?

sections.label: Transitional period for six sectors
sections.summary: The speaker says some sectors may need a transitional period due to contractual issues, with progress hoped for in two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Also, for certain sectors, it could be the transitional period required because there could be contractual issues that we need to work with from the employers' side of the house.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But, certainly, as I have mentioned in my speech earlier, for the six sectors, the majority of them, we hope to make some progress in the next two to three years.

sections.label: Retrenchment and PMET re-entry figures
sections.summary: Retrenchments rose to about 26,000 in 2020 from under 11,000 in 2019, with lower PMET re-entry within six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Total retrenchment numbers have reached an all-time high of about 26,000 in 2020, compared with just less than 11,000 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It is noteworthy that in 2019, about 60% of those retrenched were PMETs and, in the latest Q3 2020 figures, about 50% of those retrenched were PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: By the same token, about 62% of the retrenched resident PMETs re-entered the workforce within six months of their displacement in 2019 whereas in the latest Q3 2020 figures, only about 55% of retrenched resident PMETs re-entered the workforce within six months.

sections.label: Survey of PMEs on support
sections.summary: A taskforce survey of 3,500 PMEs found six in 10 wanted job loss protection and seven in 10 wanted more employment support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: A recent survey conducted by the taskforce with 3,500 PMEs across varying ages, professions and gender revealed that six in 10 PMEs felt that they needed protection against job losses, and seven in 10 expressed the need for more support in employment opportunities.

sections.label: Training survey results
sections.summary: 81% of those surveyed attended training in the last three years and 98% agreed companies should proactively send employees for training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, 81% of those surveyed attended training over the last three years and 98% agreed that companies should proactively send their employees for training to stay relevant.

sections.label: Singaporean Core access
sections.summary: Employers must ensure locals have fair access to PME roles and progression opportunities to strengthen the Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To strengthen the Singaporean Core, employers must ensure locals have fair access to PME roles and progression opportunities.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination legislation proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering anti-discrimination legislation beyond tripartite advisories to give existing institutions like TAFEP stronger enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Perhaps, it is time for us to seriously deep dive and consider, beyond mere tripartite advisories, guidelines and standards, to promulgate anti-discrimination legislation to give a stronger set of teeth to existing institutions like TAFEP which has done well in educating, promoting and encouraging fair and progressive hiring practices since its set-up.

sections.label: Unemployment insurance consideration
sections.summary: The Government set aside $100 billion to save businesses and jobs, and the speaker suggests considering unemployment insurance for retrenched workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, the Government had to set aside a budget of $100 billion to save businesses and save jobs and to provide income relief and assistance to those affected by retrenchment or severe wage cuts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In this regard, and having gleaned from the various recessions and downturns, including this current downturn, it may be timely for us to consider introducing some form of transitionary insurance, commonly referred to as unemployment insurance, to help workers affected by retrenchments and job loss.

sections.label: Three implementation hopes
sections.summary: The speaker hopes to build a Singaporean Core workforce, promulgate anti-discrimination legislation, and explore unemployment insurance for basic worker protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: When implementing the schemes and roadmaps, I hope that we can, first, build a workforce with a Singaporean Core; second, promulgate anti-discrimination legislation to eliminate workplace discrimination; third, explore the possibility of unemployment insurance so that workers can have some basic protection when unemployed.

sections.label: COVID-19 Resilience Package support
sections.summary: The speaker supports setting aside $11 billion under the COVID-19 Resilience Package, including extending the Jobs Support Scheme and COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In particular, I support the Government's proposal to set aside $11 billion under the COVID-19 Resilience Package to support workers and businesses, especially for sectors that are still under duress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The extension of the Jobs Support Scheme and the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund, for example, will go a long way to assist our brothers and sisters in the aviation, tourism and point-to-point transport sectors.

sections.label: Research spending and supercomputer ranking
sections.summary: The Government will commit 1% of GDP, about $25 billion, over five years to research and innovation, while Singapore's fastest supercomputer ranks 390th worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: While I am heartened that the Government will commit 1% of our GDP, or about $25 billion, over the next five years to invest in research and innovation, we need to ask ourselves: is this ambitious enough?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the latest list of the world's top 500 supercomputers, the processing power of Singapore's fastest supercomputer is ranked at 390th in the world.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credits usage rate
sections.summary: Less than 24% of eligible Singaporeans have utilised their SkillsFuture Credits since the scheme's launch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since its launch, less than 24% of eligible Singaporeans have utilised their SkillsFuture Credits.

sections.label: Worker transformation and flexi-work arrangements
sections.summary: The Labour Movement is committed to helping workers take on future jobs, and DBS and UOB have made flexi-work arrangements permanent post-pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Ken is a good example of a worker who is already performing a job of the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: And the Labour Movement is committed to helping every worker transform and be ready to take on the jobs of tomorrow, Mr Deputy Speaker, COVID-19 has caused a fundamental shift to our workplace culture, with many companies allowing their employees to telecommute; and local banks, such as DBS and UOB, have already committed to make flexi-work arrangements a permanent policy post-pandemic.

sections.label: Shrinking four-room HDB flat sizes
sections.summary: In the 1980s a 4-room HDB Model "A" flat had a floor area of 105 to 108 sqm, while today's new 4-room flats have 90 sqm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In the 1980s, a 4-room HDB Model "A" flat would come with a floor area of between 105 to 108 sqm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Today, new 4-room HDB flats have a floor area of 90 sqm.

sections.label: Jobs Closer to Home pilot programme
sections.summary: The new Jobs Closer to Home programme is an NTUC and Singapore Manufacturing Federation pilot to help Radin Mas residents find jobs within 5 km.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Today, I am happy to announce the new Jobs Closer to Home programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This is a pilot partnership between the NTUC and the Singapore Manufacturing Federation, to help residents in Radin Mas find jobs closer to home – more specifically, within a 5-km radius of the constituency.

sections.label: Budget support and Jobs Support Scheme
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Budget for supporting businesses and workers post-COVID-19, and is heartened by extended Jobs Support Scheme wage support for hard-hit sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, let me begin by stating that I welcome the Budget as it supports businesses and workers to adapt and grow in a post-COVID-19 world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am especially heartened by the additional wage support through the extension of Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) to support our workers in the hard-hit sectors.

sections.label: Singaporean core in energy sector
sections.summary: Union leaders report a 70% local workforce in the sector's unionised companies and over 90% in the power sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my engagements with fellow union leaders from NTUC's Oil, Petrochemical, Energy and Chemicals cluster, we do have a strong Singaporean Core in the sector's unionised companies, with a 70% local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In specifically the power sector, we have a stronger Singaporean Core with a local workforce of more than 90%.

sections.label: PWM launch in 2012
sections.summary: PWM was launched in June 2012 to let workers achieve sustainable wage increases through better skills and higher productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: PWM was launched in June 2012 to enable workers to achieve sustainable wage increases through the acquisition of better skills and higher productivity.

sections.label: PWM for Solar Energy Sector
sections.summary: NTUC is in talks to develop a PWM for the Solar Energy Sector, which would give clearer career and wage progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As shared, NTUC is in talks with the relevant stakeholders to develop a PWM for the Solar Energy Sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With Singapore aiming to achieve almost five times the current solar usage by 2030 and together with the industry career development plan for Solar Technologists, a PWM for this sector would provide a clearer career development and wage progression plan as this sector develops a Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   The extension of the Jobs Support Scheme or JSS into the aviation, aerospace and tourism sectors is truly welcomed by the trade unions in those sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They also hope that it can be extended further if the economy remains sluggish.

sections.label: Unions call for strong Singapore core
sections.summary: Labour unions call on the Government to encourage employers to build a strong Singapore core in skills, capabilities and competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Besides training, the labour unions call on the Government to encourage employers to build a strong Singapore core in their workforce not just in terms of numbers, but also in term of skills and capabilities as well as competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will be even better if the Government can incentivise employers with a strong Singaporean core in their workforce.

sections.label: Five Budgets and $100 billion
sections.summary: The Government rolled out five Budgets last year and spent close to $100 billion to help businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In order to buffer the impact, the Government rolled out five Budgets last year and spent close to $100 billion to help businesses cut costs and to help workers save jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: If not for that decisive and massive action, the GDP drop last year would not be the minus 5.4%; it would be something more like minus 12.4%.

sections.label: Reserves once spent
sections.summary: The $100 billion from our reserves, once it is spent, it is spent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The $100 billion from our reserves, once it is spent, it is spent.

sections.label: Senior worker employment rates
sections.summary: Employment rate for those 65 and above rose 0.9 percentage points from 2019, but senior workers in aerospace, aviation and retail faced non-renewals of re-employment contracts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In fact, for the age band 65 and above, the employment rate last year went up by 0.9-percentage points, compared to 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: At the same time, Mr Deputy Speaker, I must also point out that for the distressed sectors such as aerospace, aviation and retail, senior workers have experienced significant impact through non-offers or non-renewals of re-employment contracts as the firms downsized.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers agreed to raise the retirement age from 62 to 65 and re-employment ceiling from 67 to 70, starting July 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Government responded positively to our call and set up the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers, which then reached consensus to raise the Statutory Retirement Age from 62 to 65, and the re-employment age ceiling from 67 to 70 progressively over the coming decade, starting with a new retirement age of 63 and a new re-employment age ceiling of 68 from July 2022.

sections.label: Civil Service retirement ages
sections.summary: The Civil Service raised its officers' retirement and re-employment ages by one year to 63 and 68 in July, a year ahead of the national schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: As an employer ourselves, we have taken the lead.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We have raised the organisational retirement age and re-employment age ceiling by one year from 1 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Civil Service announced in 2019 that it will raise the retirement and re-employment ages of its officers by one year to 63 and 68 respectively in July this year – again, a year ahead of the national schedule.

sections.label: Deferred CPF enhancements
sections.summary: COVID-19 disrupted the economy, forcing planned CPF enhancements to be deferred by a year to 1 January 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, COVID-19 disrupted our whole economy, forcing the planned CPF enhancements to be deferred by a year, to 1 January 2022.

sections.label: Raising retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: The speaker calls for the July 2022 raising of retirement and re-employment ages and the deferred January 2022 CPF improvements to proceed without further delay.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must be careful not to kick the can down the road further because if we negatively impact on retirement adequacy, that will come back to bite us earlier and harder.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I am therefore calling for the planned raising of the Statutory Retirement and Re-employment Ages in July 2022, as well as with the agreed deferred improvements to the CPF contributions now due in January 2022, to be proceeded with, without further delay.

sections.label: Flexible Work Arrangements adoption
sections.summary: The speaker urges Government to support more pervasive adoption of Flexible Work Arrangements instead of lapsing back to full-time workplace arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We must build on this insight and make gains, and not just lapse back into the status quo and go back into the same-old, same-old of must be here at the workplace and must be full-time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I therefore urge Government to strongly support the more pervasive adoption of Flexible Work Arrangements.

sections.label: ITM and CTC integration
sections.summary: The speaker urges further integration between Industry Transformation Maps jobs-skills ladders and Company Training Committees, and more resourcing for CTCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Only that action will give us the results that we need.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I therefore urge further integration between the jobs-skills ladders of the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) and the work of Company Training Committees (CTCs), including the sectoral versions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The CTCs are equipped to help companies undertake Operations-Technology-Skills road-mapping.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I think we should do more in order to resource them so that they can propagate even faster.

sections.label: National Adult Immunisation Schedule
sections.summary: MOH established the National Adult Immunisation Schedule in November 2017, and the speaker urges leveraging vaccination for business resilience and senior worker health.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: MOH established what is called the National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS) in November 2017 – that was pre-COVID-19 – in order to provide guidance on vaccinations that persons aged 18 years or older should adopt to protect themselves against vaccine-preventable diseases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In the light of the COVID-19 experience, I think the usefulness of this schedule has become much more salient.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I urge Government and the tripartite partners to work together to see how best to leverage science-based cost-effective vaccination to enhance business resilience and senior worker health.

sections.label: Use of $100 billion
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the $100 billion used by the Finance Minister was well used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Imagine if I tell you now your last 10 years of your own savings or you had to use it all up in one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But the $100 billion that the Finance Minister used, was it well used?

sections.label: Digital divide in rental flats
sections.summary: Research showed 44% of families in rental units lacked a connection and 44% lacked a computer or laptop, prompting an iPad loan scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Research on a representative sample of Singaporeans has shown that 44% families who lived in rental units, they did not have a connection, and another 44% lacked a computer or a laptop at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And which is why when my hat as the Group CEO of NTUC Enterprise, at our NTUC First Campus, just two months ago, we launched a scheme to loan iPads to more than 2,000 low-income families and their children attending our My First Skool centres to help them bridge this digital divide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I think it may be worth looking at this more closely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, of all the families who are living in rental flats with school-going children, how many do not have a PC, and how many do not have broadband connections?

sections.label: Free broadband for low-income households
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider giving all low-income households, especially those with school-going children, free broadband connections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I think this is a very useful and helpful scheme that can be greatly expanded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So I urge the Government to consider giving all low-income households, especially those with school-going children, free broadband connections.

sections.label: $20 million ComChest matching fund
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced a $20 million fund to match Community Chest donations raised through spontaneous acts daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng has announced that a $20 million fund will be set aside to match the Community Chest (ComChest) donations raised through spontaneous acts daily.

sections.label: SIRS COVID-19 self-employed payouts
sections.summary: SIRS gave self-employed people three quarterly $3,000 payouts, open to those earning up to $100,000 net trade income and living in property with annual value up to $21,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: SIRS, as you know, is a COVID-19 assistance programme which provided self-employed people with three quarterly cash payouts of $3,000 each in May, July and October and it is opened to those who earned a net trade income of up to $100,000 and live in a property with an annual value of no more than $21,000.

sections.label: NTUC FairPrice mature workforce demographics
sections.summary: NTUC FairPrice's workforce is 66% over 40, 46% over 50 and 22% over 60, outperforming national workforce demographics, which the speaker calls a strength.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We are proud that we have a very strong local core at all levels – management as well as rank and file.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And look at the demographics of our workforce at our largest social enterprise, NTUC Fairprice, our mature workforce speaks of our value system and we see it as a strength: 66% of our staff, that is about two-thirds, are more than 40 years old; 46% are more than 50 years old and 22% more than 60 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And we have quite a few who are over 70 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: These statistics all outperform the national workforce demographics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All said, every worker, young and old, every worker matters.

sections.label: Women in elected parliamentary seats
sections.summary: Of 93 elected Member of Parliament seats, 29% belong to women, compared to just four seats two decades ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Out of the 93 seats for elected Members of Parliament, 29% of the elected seats belong to women, compared to just four seats two decades ago.

sections.label: Petrol duty increase for drivers
sections.summary: The petrol duty increase means drivers pay another 10 cents per litre, requiring more driving hours amid low street hails from absent tourism and closed night spots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The petrol duties increase effectively means that for our drivers, they pay another 10 cents per litre of petrol that they need for their livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While the urgent need to go green for national security is definitely something that is not lost on our sisters, this 10 cents per litre, means that they would need to spend more long gruelling hours driving their taxis, this made all the more challenging with street hails at a low due to the dearth of tourism and night spots remaining closed.

sections.label: COVID Drivers Relief Fund concerns
sections.summary: The community appreciates the six-month $3,150 COVID Drivers Relief Fund and expedited rebates but worries what happens once support ends.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The community appreciates the six-month $3,150 COVID Drivers Relief Fund (CDRF) and is heartened by the close tripartite relationship that brought along the expedited disbursement of the tax and additional petrol duty rebates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But our community is still worried that the COVID-19 situation will stretch beyond six months and would like to know what would happen once the support ends.

sections.label: Respite care for women workers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes publicly available in-community registry of professional care-givers for eldercare, childcare and cleaning, giving women short-term care access.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we recognise the pressures faced by our women warriors, I put forth that there might be a need to provide support for respite care that might alleviate the burdens of our women workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: An in-community registry of professional care-givers, who could help with eldercare, childcare, and even cleaning services could be made publicly available for women to access short-term care in community easily.

sections.label: Awareness, respite care subsidies
sections.summary: Unions hope to promote awareness of employment practices, and additional subsidies are needed to help primary care-givers with respite care costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Over the next few months, the unions hope that with the support of the Government, we will be able to promote more wide spread awareness to better employment practices and understanding the expectations and aspirations of our women employers and their hired help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, although respite care options are available, they might not be affordable for certain families that already carry the burden of expensive medical bills and daily expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Thus, it presents itself as necessary for there to be additional subsidies to help primary care-givers relieve the financial burden of seeking assistance.

sections.label: Singapore Centre for Working Women
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a Singapore Centre for Working Women as a resource and safe space for women, with the Labour Movement's support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Looking at the world through the lens of our women, their dreams, aspirations, grievances, and indeed, their humanity, has led me to dream up the possibilities created by having a Singapore Centre for Working Women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Imagine, a single resource centre for women, covering everything I have spoken about in the past 15 minutes and more, where women can come to explore new livelihood options, air grievances, seek mentorship, access best practices, apply for support, seek redress, form alliances and of course, to assist and guide along other women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is my hope for our women warriors to have a safe space to be themselves amidst other women warriors – a place where women can be unabashedly themselves, unashamed to seek help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And in these connections, be empowered to be the best versions of themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is by capturing the diversity of the concerns and aspirations of our women warriors that we may best release their potential.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement will be here to walk with you on your journey, protect you, and help you reach for the stars.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive extension
sections.summary: The Jobs Growth Incentive saw more than 110,000 local hires last year, and the speaker fully supports its extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) has seen extremely promising results – with more than 110,000 local hires last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is clearly an important measure in shoring up local hiring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I fully support the extension of the JGI.

sections.label: SGUnited Traineeships extension
sections.summary: The speaker supports extending SGUnited Traineeships until 31 March 2022, noting such traineeships made up 16.9% of graduates employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Second, I support the Government's move to extend the SGUnited Traineeships until 31 March 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the annual Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey, SGUnited Traineeships made up 16.9% of graduates who found employment.

sections.label: Platform workers' protection issues
sections.summary: Three issues are named for workers dependent on platform companies: no key employment legislation protection, insufficient social protection, and lack of upgrading incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is especially important as workers dependent on large platform companies or organisations as their primary source of income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: There are three salient issues to be tackled: platform workers are unprotected by key employment legislation, there is insufficient social protection and the lack of incentives to upgrade this segment of the workforce.

sections.label: Fairness for platform workers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests letting unions represent platform workers collectively or giving them statutory protection under the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I believe that more can be done to level the playing field between workers and platform companies to ensure that parties are treated fairly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I suggest that we can consider either allowing the Union to represent these workers collectively or to provide these workers with some level of statutory protection under this Employment Act.

sections.label: CPF contributions and state support
sections.summary: With no CPF contributions from employers and employees, the state will eventually have to shoulder social support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Because there are no CPF contributions from both employers and employees, the state will have to shoulder social support eventually.

sections.label: Cost-sharing with platform companies
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider cost-sharing schemes with platform companies to encourage training support for these workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Government look into cost-sharing schemes with platform companies to encourage training support for these workers?

sections.label: 2020 Budget grants and jobs
sections.summary: According to MOF, $27.4 billion in grants across the five 2020 Budgets saved or created 155,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over the course of the five Budgets in 2020, according to MOF, $27.4 billion in grants were used to shore beleaguered companies; 155,000 jobs were saved or created.

sections.label: Suggestions to cut expenditure
sections.summary: Some suggest reducing expenditure on education, public amenities and defence so more money can be given as cash assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On the other hand, there are some who suggest that we reduce expenditure in areas such as education, public amenities and even defence, so that more money can be given out as cash assistance.

sections.label: Taxing tech and online sales
sections.summary: Australia agreed with media tech companies to collect tax on news and European countries taxed online goods; possible tax revenue sources can be explored with tech companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Just a few hours ago this morning, Australia's government had reached agreement with media tech companies to collect tax on news while European countries have imposed tax on goods sold online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We can work with tech companies to look at possible sources of tax revenue, such as advertising revenue, whilst we continue to welcome and incentivise their investment here.

sections.label: Speeding up hardship schemes
sections.summary: Some waited over three months; agencies must swiftly administer hardship schemes, and job growth incentives, job credits, wage supplements and SGUnited outreach should continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some of them had to wait for more than three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Government agencies must put in place measures to ensure that all these schemes to ease hardship be swiftly and effectively administered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I welcome the extension of job growth incentives to support the employment of Singaporeans, especially the seniors and people with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I appeal for further extension of job credits and wage supplements, which have been well received by Singaporeans, to support senior workers and low-income workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centre should continue to reach out to new graduates in the next three years, so that they, too, will have certainty in the post-COVID-19 world.

sections.label: GST on online purchases
sections.summary: The speaker supports GST on online purchases to level the playing field and calls electric vehicle support timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Examples include online food delivery and online conferences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I support GST on purchases made online to level the playing field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The supporting measures for electric vehicles are timely.

sections.label: Childcare support leave extension
sections.summary: The speaker appeals for extension of childcare support leave for working parents without family support during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Last but not least, in view of the pandemic, I appeal for extension of childcare support leave for working parents who do not have family support to look after their children.

sections.label: Jobs at risk of redundancy
sections.summary: The WEF Future of Jobs Report 2020 noted accountants, auditors, bank tellers and HR specialists were at highest redundancy risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum (WEF) Future of Jobs Report 2020 noted that accountants, auditors, bank tellers and HR specialists were at the highest risk of redundancy.

sections.label: Discouraged workers share 2020
sections.summary: Discouraged workers were 0.7% of the resident labour force in 2020, above the 2009 high of 0.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Discouraged workers made up 0.7% of the resident labour force in 2020, surpassing the previous high of 0.6% in the 2009 GFC recession; 0.7% is not yet a tsunami by any means but it is a sobering bellwether.

sections.label: Singapore market versus US markets
sections.summary: In 2020 the Straits Times Index weakened while NASDAQ rose 42% and S&P 500 rose 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2020, when the Straits Times Index was severely weakened due to COVID-19, the US NASDAQ went up 42% and the wider S&P 500 was up 15% at the end of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As my Parliamentary colleague Mr Louis Chua mentioned yesterday, return on equity for the Singapore market, ex-financials, has also seen a steady decline, falling to a 20-year low of 5.9% in 2019, before COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the fourth quarter of 2019, 35% of firms listed in Singapore were already loss making, the highest level since the 2008/2009 global financial crisis.

sections.label: Employees unimpressed by AI policies
sections.summary: Over 60% of employees and managers in a 2019 survey were unimpressed or undecided about Government AI job policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To take another example, despite concerted policy efforts to digitise, more than 60% of employees and managers in Singapore firms in a 2019 survey said that they were unimpressed or undecided about Government policies in preparation for the impact of Artificial Intelligence on jobs.

sections.label: Graduate unemployment and infocomm jobs
sections.summary: Six months after graduation, around 12% were unemployed and over 30% were in part-time or temporary jobs, while the education system produces 2,800 infocomm graduates yearly against 60,000 new infocomm jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Six months after graduation, around 12% were unemployed and over 30% were in part-time or temporary jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan said last year that there will be 60,000 new jobs created in the infocomm sector over just the next three years, but our education system is only producing 2,800 infocomm graduates yearly.

sections.label: Fresh graduates in temporary employment
sections.summary: More than one in five fresh graduates from the four local Autonomous Universities were in part-time or temporary employment in 2020, rising from 7% in 2019 to 22.3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More than one in five fresh graduates from our four local Autonomous Universities were in part-time or temporary employment in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a proportion of the newly graduated workforce, they more than tripled from 7% in 2019 to 22.3% in 2020.

sections.label: Engaging disruptive sector companies
sections.summary: The speaker asks how economic agencies can engage companies in disruptive industry sectors with no physical presence in Singapore to take on Singaporeans for traineeships and internships such as SGUnited Traineeship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to speak about how our economic agencies can possibly engage companies in disruptive industry sectors who have no physical presence in Singapore as yet, to take on Singaporeans for traineeships and internships such as the SGUnited Traineeship.

sections.label: Including companies in programmes
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether some of these companies can be considered for inclusion in such programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can we consider including some of these companies in such programmes?

sections.label: Transferable SkillsFuture credits
sections.summary: The speaker repeats a call to enable SkillsFuture credits to be transferable among family members, a subject on which a Parliamentary Question was previously filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Before I leave the subject of skills training, I would like to repeat my call to enable SkillsFuture credits to be transferable among family members, a subject on which I have filed a Parliamentary Question previously.

sections.label: Benchmarking work conditions
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOM and MTI benchmark conditions of work in other developed countries for sectors struggling to find Singaporeans, particularly low-wage sectors, to identify gaps and work with industry bodies to plug them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My point is that even if we increase pay, Singaporeans may not want these jobs if they perceive that conditions of work are not good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would suggest that in sectors where we struggle to find enough Singaporeans, particularly low-wage sectors, the MOM and MTI benchmark conditions of work in other developed countries where there are more locals employed at higher productivity levels in that sector, to understand what the gaps are in conditions of work, and take steps to work with industry bodies to plug those gaps.

sections.label: Timing of petrol duties GST
sections.summary: Many have questioned the timing of the petrol duty hike and GST on small-value imported items given the fragile economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Many have questioned the timing of the hike in petrol duties and the levying of GST on small-value imported items, given the fragile state the economy is still in.

sections.label: Win-win approaches to outcomes
sections.summary: It is useful for all, not only Government, to bear in mind that there are win-win approaches to drive towards these outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And it is useful for all of us to bear this in mind – not only in Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are win-win approaches to drive towards these outcomes.

sections.label: Auditing policies and publishing results
sections.summary: Existing cultures and mindsets exist for a reason, and schemes should not become black boxes; policies should be audited and results published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Existing cultures and mindsets, existing behaviour patterns are there for a reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such as, work conditions for jobs that Singaporeans shun that I spoke about earlier, and try to fix them with the tools that we have, so as to catalyse change in cultures and mindsets.
