sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, Sir, let us never allow schemes to become black boxes into which fiscal resources get poured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Let us rigorously audit the impact of our policies and budget and plan for such measurement and publish the results to support informed public debate, consensus formation and genuine policy co-creation.

sections.label: Service buyers as employers
sections.summary: Under the Workplace Safety and Health Act, a service buyer is treated as an employer, sharing responsibility for outsourced workers with service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the Workplace Safety and Health Act (or WSHA), a service buyer at whose premises outsourced workers are deployed, is treated as an employer, with all of the duties and responsibilities incumbent on an employer under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In other words, service buyers and service providers share responsibility for outsourced workers at site.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, because outsourced workers do not work at their employer’s premises but that of the service buyers, their conditions of work are determined primarily by service buyers.

sections.label: Condo refused workers toilet use
sections.summary: In January last year, the Security Association alerted the speaker that an ultra-luxury condominium along Grange Road refused outsourced workers use of any toilet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In January last year, Sir, I was alerted through the Security Association that at an ultra-luxury condominium along Grange Road had refused to allow outsourced workers to use any toilet in the condominium.

sections.label: Workfare grant for rest areas
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Zaqy announced in Parliament last year a workfare grant to be launched in 2020 to support rest areas for outsourced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy announced in Parliament last year that a workfare grant would be launched in 2020 to support building owners and employers to provide rest areas for outsourced workers.

sections.label: Security officers' work week changes
sections.summary: Officers previously worked six-day weeks; from this year they may work two 5-day and two 6-day weeks monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Up to the beginning of this year, officers generally would work six-day weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From this year, officers have a possible work permutation where they can work two 5-day weeks and two 6-day weeks in a month.

sections.label: Proposed shift lengths
sections.summary: The speaker views eight to 10-hour shifts as more reasonable, with eight hours for day shifts and nine to 10 for night shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My view is that it is more reasonable to have eight to 10-hour shifts – eight hours for the day shifts, which are generally more busy; and nine to 10 hours for the night shift.

sections.label: Regularising security officers' working hours
sections.summary: The speaker calls on tripartite partners to work towards regularising security officers' working hours towards eight to 10-hour shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I call on the tripartite partners to work towards regularising working hours of security officers towards eight to 10- hour shifts.

sections.label: Estimated workers benefiting
sections.summary: By the speaker's estimates from publicly available data, the measures will apply to and benefit around 120,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By my estimates, based on publicly available data, Sir, these measures will apply to, and benefit, around 120,000 workers.

sections.label: One Million Trees plan details
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee said the one million trees will sequester an estimated 78,000 tonnes of carbon, with 1,000 hectares set aside, 200 for new nature parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In response to our Parliamentary Question I filed earlier this year, Minister Desmond Lee shared that the one million trees to be planted under the Plan will sequester an estimated 78,000 tonnes of carbon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under the Plan, the Government aims to set aside one thousand hectares for green spaces of which 200 hectares will be for new nature parks.

sections.label: Transport emissions breakdown
sections.summary: Transport is the third largest emissions sector at about 15.7%, with diesel roughly 63% and petrol 33% of transport emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Transport is the third largest sector from which our greenhouse gas emissions from fuel combustion are derived, accounting for about 15.7% of our emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Of these, the biggest contributors are the use of diesel, accounting for roughly 63% of transport emissions, and the use of petrol, accounting for 33%.

sections.label: EV charging points target increase
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Deputy Prime Minister's Budget announcement to raise the EV charging point target from 28,000 to 60,000 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I had asked whether we should even be contented with this ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the Deputy Prime Minister's announcement in his Budget speech last week that the Government now plans to increase the number of charging points for EVs from the original target of 28,000 to 60,000 by 2030.

sections.label: ICE phase-out and petrol duty
sections.summary: The Government aims to phase out ICE vehicles by 2040, with over 900,000 vehicles on the roads, and announced a petrol duty increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Previously, the Government has said it aims to phase out all ICE vehicles by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This endeavour is by no means a small one given that I believe we have more than 900,000, almost a million vehicles, on our roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Further, while the Government announced last year that all newly purchased public buses will be electric or hybrid in nature, when does it envisage that our entire bus fleet will be fully electric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced in this year's Budget that he is going to increase the petrol duty.

sections.label: Call to review petrol tax hike
sections.summary: The speaker repeats the Leader of the Opposition's call for the Government to review the petrol tax hike and phase it in with EV usage growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, I hope while this abrupt increase may not be what we say in Chinese: 落进下石, it is certainly 雪上加霜 for many.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, I repeat the call made by the Leader of the Opposition, the hon Member Mr Pritam Singh, for the Government to review this hike and to phase in the petrol tax hike in proportion to the actual growth of EV usage on the roads.

sections.label: Manufacturing and construction emissions share
sections.summary: Singapore's manufacturing and construction industries account for about 38.8% of total greenhouse gas emissions, second after the energy sector's 41.87%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our manufacturing and construction industries account for about 38.8% of total greenhouse gas emissions, the second largest sector after our energy sector which contributes about 41.87%.

sections.label: CDC vouchers for Singapore households
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced the Government will partner CDCs to give all Singapore households $100 in CDC vouchers for participating shops and hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: First, Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced in his Budget speech that the Government will partner the Community Development Councils (CDCs) to give all Singapore households $100 worth of CDC vouchers to be used at participating shops and hawker centres.

sections.label: Rental relief and property tax rebate
sections.summary: The Government provided up to $900 million in cash grants to landlords for rental relief, and landlords also receive $1.8 billion in property tax rebate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: To its credit, the Government stepped in to provide up to $900 million in cash grants to landlords for rental relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In addition, the landlords also receive $1.8 billion dollars in property tax rebate.

sections.label: SME rental support taper
sections.summary: The speaker says current support slows SME recovery and may entrench MNCs and GLCs, and asks for tapered rental support for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This only slows down the recovery for SMEs and could have the undesirable effect of entrenching the positions of multinational corporations (MNCs) and Government-linked Corporations (GLCs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I call upon the Government to see if there is scope to have tapered support for SMEs in rentals over this period.

sections.label: Women's pandemic job losses
sections.summary: In Latin America women were 50% more likely than men to lose jobs in the pandemic's first month, and female job losses were 1.8 times higher in the US and India.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In Latin America, women were 50% more likely than men to lose a job in the pandemic’s first month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: McKinsey also reported that female job losses is 1.8 times higher than male job losses in the US and India.

sections.label: Support for senior employment
sections.summary: Government initiatives such as the Special Employment Credit and Retirement and Re-Employment Act support senior employment, and CPF contribution rate increments for workers above 55 were announced in August 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Over the past years, much has been done to better support senior employment in Singapore, with Government initiatives such as the Special Employment Credit and Retirement and Re-Employment Act introduced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: CPF contribution rate increment for workers above the age of 55 was also announced in August 2019.

sections.label: Randstad survey on ageism
sections.summary: Randstad's 2020 survey on workplace ageism found 57% of Singaporeans feel training opportunities decrease with age, and 64% of those aged 55 and above feel this way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Recruitment agency Randstad reported in a 2020 survey on ageism in the workplace that 57% of Singaporeans feel training opportunities get fewer as they grow older and 64% of those aged 55 and above feel this way.

sections.label: Measures for older workers
sections.summary: Singapore introduced the Special Employment Credit and Retirement and Re-employment Act, and announced in August 2019 increased CPF contribution rates for workers aged 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Over the last few years, Singapore has introduced measures such as the Special Employment Credit and Retirement and Re-employment Act to support the employment of older Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Government also announced in August 2019 an increase in CPF contribution rates for workers aged 55 and above.

sections.label: Digital fluency and gender gaps
sections.summary: A 2016 Accenture report found digital fluency can accelerate closing gender gaps, with countries achieving gender equality 25 to 40 years faster.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: A 2016 Accenture report found that digital fluency can accelerate the closing of gender gaps, as countries can achieve gender equality some 25 to 40 years faster.

sections.label: Women in Singapore technology
sections.summary: A BCG study found Singapore's women in technology at about 41%, while female technology graduates lag at 29%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Based on a study conducted by the Boston Consulting Group (BCG), Singapore’s woman representation in technology is about 41%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Notably, however, Singapore female university graduates who studied technology lags behind other Southeast Asian countries at only 29%.

sections.label: Promoting women in tech
sections.summary: The speaker cites SG Women in Tech and PayPal's Women Luminaries Programme and proposes four ways to further support women in tech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But Nurul's experience is perhaps not a common one, yet.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Now and then, I still receive requests for help or hear of stories from residents who completed courses and tried hard to switch to a career in tech but were unsuccessful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To be fair, Singapore has, in recent years, stepped up our effort to promote women in tech with initiatives, such as SG Women in Tech by the IMDA and the Women Luminaries Programme by PayPal and our four local Autonomous Universities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But, we can do more to: one, introduce more scholarships and education awards to encourage girls to study technology and related subjects in school; two, continue to emphasise public commitment to cultivating girls and women in tech in Singapore; three, drive board agendas and have companies set goals to recruit and cultivate more women in tech roles, and create environments that are enabling for talents, both men and women alike, with family commitments; and four, create and facilitate more peer-networking and mentoring platforms for women or aspiring women in tech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Government's effort in addressing gaps, ensuring fair distribution of resources and opportunities and engendering an inclusive society cannot be understated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But I believe we can still do more to help Singaporeans emerge stronger and feel that they are stronger, not weaker.

sections.label: FY2021 Budget deficit
sections.summary: A $31 billion basic deficit is offset by half the $39.2 billion NIR, giving an $11 billion overall deficit for FY2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The basic deficit of $31 billion is attributable to $11 billion for the Resilience Package and $24 billion spread over three years for the emerging stronger initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This basic deficit can be easily covered by the NIR or Net Investment Return earned from our total financial assets of more than $1.35 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This NIR is estimated to be $39.2 billion for FY2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, since the Government's policy is to only use half of the NIR for spending every year, we can only use $19.6 billion to offset the basic deficit, which gives us an overall Budget deficit of $11 billion for FY2021.

sections.label: Reliance on foreign labour
sections.summary: Quoting Yeoh Lam Keong on dependence on foreign capital and labour, the speaker criticises the Budget's S Pass quota adjustment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Yeoh Lam Keong, the former GIC Chief Economist and one of the founders of FOSG or the Future of Singapore Group, has pointed out that, and I quote, "our most fundamental economic weaknesses stem (from) our structural excessive dependence on foreign capital and foreign labour." So, in preparing for a post-COVID-19 future, should we not seize this opportunity to reduce our reliance on foreign labour?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I was disappointed that the Budget only adjusted the S Pass quota for the manufacturing sector for managing the local-foreign worker mix.

sections.label: Higher 2021 premiums
sections.summary: In 2021 Singaporeans will pay up to 35% more in MediShield Life premiums and begin paying CareShield premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2021, Singaporeans will not only have to pay up to 35% more in MediShield Life premiums, but will also have to start paying CareShield premiums.

sections.label: Proposed living wage
sections.summary: A living wage of $1,500 take-home pay, or $2,055 gross, is proposed, with Government paying most of the increase from 2021 to 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Using this benchmark, we propose a living wage of $1,500 take-home pay for all local workers which translates into $2,055 in gross wages for a start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government could pay the main portion of the increase from 2021 to 2023 to allow businesses time to adjust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We estimate this will increase operating expenditure by about $1.6 billion in each of the next three years.

sections.label: Monthly levy on EP holders
sections.summary: It recommends a $1,200 monthly levy on all EP holders immediately, estimated to generate $2.7 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It has often been highlighted that this is a loophole for employers to exploit to the disadvantage of our Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, in order to level the playing field, we recommend imposing a $1,200 monthly levy on all EP holders immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The $1,200 amount is based on the employer's contribution and part of the employee's contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is estimated to generate new operating revenue of $2.7 billion per annum.

sections.label: CPF members and Basic Retirement Sum
sections.summary: About half of CPF members do not have enough money even to satisfy the $93,000 Basic Retirement Sum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In reality, about half of the CPF members do not have enough money in their CPF account, even to satisfy the Basic Retirement Sum of $93,000.

sections.label: Funding MediShield Life and CareShield premiums
sections.summary: It recommends Government funding of MediShield Life and CareShield premiums for all Singaporeans and PRs, costing $2.6 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, we recommend that the Government funds, the insurance premiums of the MediShield Life and CareShield scheme for all Singaporeans and PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will increase operating expenditure by adjustable justifiable some of $2.6 billion per annum, which is only 0.5% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: By taking away one of the sources of drain on the CPF funds, most Singaporeans will be able to satisfy the basic retirement sum of $93,000, and also not to have to worry about the unaffordable premiums in their old age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This means that two social security problems of Singaporeans are resolved by one policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And if we relax, the withdrawal limit for MediSave at the same time, because more cash is now available in the account, we will resolve another financial problem for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Reallocating resources or additional spending
sections.summary: The Government can reallocate existing resources to these recommendations or let the additional spending stimulate the recovering economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government can decide whether it wants to reallocate existing resources to these recommendations, or allow the additional spending to provide more stimulus for the recovering economy.

sections.label: Review of EP qualifying criteria
sections.summary: The Singapore Government reviews the EP qualifying criteria constantly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government reviews the EP qualifying criteria constantly.

sections.label: Blanket levy and foreign investors
sections.summary: A blanket levy on EP holders signals to foreign investors that we do not quite welcome them bringing their own talent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: A blanket levy on EP holders is a signal to foreign investors that we do not quite welcome them bringing in their own talent.

sections.label: Foreign investment and Singaporean jobs
sections.summary: Restricting companies to hiring Singaporeans for top jobs could drive them away and lose good jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: If we start telling companies that they can invest but can only employ Singaporeans for the top jobs, we will end up chasing some of them away and thousands of good jobs for Singaporeans will be lost as well.

sections.label: Rebalancing foreign workforce top positions
sections.summary: The speaker says rebalancing is too slow, with over 40% foreigners in the workforce and many in top positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: However, what we are pointing out, as in my maiden speech in September last year, we need a rebalancing, and we think the rebalancing is going on too slowly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Now, with more than 40% of the foreigners in our workforce, many of them have taken over the top positions.

sections.label: MAS officials KPI
sections.summary: The passage states it does not appear to be a KPI for MAS officials today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Today, it does not seem to be even a KPI for the MAS officials.

sections.label: Foreigners in retail banking executives
sections.summary: The passage asks why senior executive positions in retail banking still have 30% to 40% foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Like for example, the senior executive positions in the retail banking sector in Singapore, why should there still be 30% to 40% of foreigners?

sections.label: Retail bank managers foreigners share
sections.summary: The passage asks why 30% of retail bank managers are foreigners and notes the PSP's position and the Government's different view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Why are 30% of retail bank managers still foreigners?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are 70% and a much larger pie with a larger share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is the essence of being an open and international financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, I think I have also come to the same conclusion as Minister of State Gan Siow Huang that actually the PSP's position is that you want Singapore to close up and protect the jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is entitled to that view, but I think the Government and MAS have a different view.

sections.label: Extending Singapore Government Securities maturity
sections.summary: The passage says extending debt maturity under SINGA to 50 or 100 years should not be ruled out to lock in low rates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, while the maturities of existing Singapore Government Securities run from two to 30 years, we should not rule out the possibility of further extending the maturity of debt issued under the auspices of SINGA, to 50 or 100 years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would lock in the currently very favourable low rates for a much longer period as befitting truly long-term projects.

sections.label: Benchmarking debt issuance speed
sections.summary: Debt issuance speed should be benchmarked against prevailing growth conditions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, it is important to benchmark the speed of debt issuance against prevailing growth conditions.

sections.label: Interest rate versus growth rate
sections.summary: If the interest rate routinely exceeds the growth rate, attention is warranted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One is that if the interest rate begins to routinely exceed the growth rate, we want to pay attention.

sections.label: Hard capital versus soft capital
sections.summary: The cited examples are hard capital, but long-term investments in people's capabilities, or soft capital, should also be considered.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Undeniably, the examples cited above are excellent examples of hard capital, which extend the promise of raising productivity and growth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But, why would we limit our investments to only bridges and train lines and airports and seawalls, and not consider the equally important long-term investments we could direct toward soft capital, namely the capabilities of our people?

sections.label: Research and development expenditure
sections.summary: R&D is an area to spend more on, as Singapore devotes just under 2% of income to it, behind Israel, Japan and South Korea.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One important area where we can afford to spend more is in terms of research and development expenditure (R&D).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We currently only devote a little less than 2% of our income toward R&D efforts, behind leading innovation nations such as Israel, Japan and South Korea.

sections.label: Classroom sizes versus peers

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our classrooms, at 33 students across most subjects, are a full 10 children in excess of the average class size of our industrial economy peers.

sections.label: SINGA borrowing authorisation increase
sections.summary: The amount authorised for total borrowing under SINGA should be increased by $60 billion or carved out of the proposed $90 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To that end, I propose that the amount to be authorised for total borrowing under SINGA, either be increased by $60 billion or to be carved out of the proposed $90 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Importantly, even if we take the $60 and $90 billion together, this would represent a little less than a third of our GDP, an eminently sustainable debt burden, especially at low rates and when earmarked for investments with high long-term payoffs.

sections.label: Extension of GSS support
sections.summary: Minister Heng suggested short-term spending plans include extending GSS support for Tier-1 and certain Tier-2 corporations.

sentences.text: Minister Heng had suggested that our short-term spending plans will include an extension of GSS support Tier-1 corporations for another six months and certain Tier-2 corporations for another three.

sections.label: Support for the Motion

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these additional suggestions and those that I plan to raise in the Committee of Supply, I support the Motion.

sections.label: Joey's business support outcomes

sentences.text: She managed to retain all her workers and has not had to retrench anyone yet.

sections.label: Singapore women workforce participation

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: At the height of the pandemic, the employment rate for females remained at about 73.2%.

sections.label: Prof Leo Yee-Sin's outbreak leadership
sections.summary: Prof Leo Yee-Sin, Executive Director of the National Centre for Infectious Diseases, led Singapore through multiple outbreaks.

sentences.text: We also have Prof Leo Yee-Sin who is the Executive Director of the National Centre for Infectious Diseases.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)

sentences.text: About 65% of the recipients are women who had low earnings throughout their lives and now have less in retirement.

sections.label: Sun Xueling on Budget 2021 women

sentences.text: While I am glad to hear that about $200 million increase in budget allocation will be given for the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and Part-time Re-employment Grant from Deputy Prime Minister Heng, care for seniors must also extend to supporting them to age in place.

sections.label: Over-subscribed BTO pilot project

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This BTO project, which was over-subscribed by 4.2 times shows that there is a demand for such kind of apartments.

sections.label: Issues raised during COVID-19 pandemic

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From my interactions, the issues they care deeply about, during this COVID-19 pandemic are jobs and the economy, the support of vulnerable groups in the community, environmental sustainability and mental wellness.

sections.label: Low-income youths and petrol duty hikes

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The introduction of the petrol duty hikes, though needed for the good of the environment, maybe a bit too abrupt for many to adjust to, especially if they are from low-income families.

sections.label: Inclusion and care-giver support
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Inclusive Support Programme and Alliances for Action on support for care-givers of persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There may be inherent systemic, structural barriers that make it difficult for them to contribute their voices, so we must make a conscious effort to recognise those barriers and break them down so that their voices are heard.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also truly feel that the Alliances for Action on support for care-givers of persons with disabilities is a step in the right direction and echoes what the youths have been seeking.

sections.label: Suicides and mental wellness taskforce
sections.summary: The speaker notes rising suicides, welcomes the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce, and asks about updates or budget.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Samaritans of Singapore, the number of suicides rose 10% in 2020, with suicides among boys aged 10 to 19 at a record high.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is worrying, as according to mental health professionals, stresses relating to the social and economic impact of the pandemic may have an impact on mental wellness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome that the Government has set up a COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce to tackle the pandemic’s impact on mental health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I would like to know if there are any updates or if a budget is allocated to take this further moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Malay population has a relatively higher youth base with 32% of its population between ages 15 and 34, as compared to national at 26%.

sections.label: Developing Malay youth leadership

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, we need to tap on our promising Malay youths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe the Budget should try to further leverage on this, by providing more platforms to develop their leadership potential and volunteer with the community.

sections.label: Youths and Budget future choices
sections.summary: The speaker tells youths their values and choices shape Singapore's future and urges them to use their voice on the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The intention you have in your heart, the values you embody and the choices that you make form who you are and what we become as a society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If you choose to be kind, compassionate, inclusive, fair and brave, then that is the Singapore you will build for the future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Youths, the Budget is about the kind of future that you want.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is about the kind of country that you believe in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, sit up, take note, understand it, use your voice.

sections.label: Pre-school, elder and disability care
sections.summary: The Government will raise pre-school places to 80% and expand elder, respite and residential care, with an Alliances for Action on care-givers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government will raise the proportion of Government-supported pre-school places to 80% in four years' time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Similarly, a range of affordable and quality elder and respite care services will be made more accessible to lighten the financial and physical burden of caring for our elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For the elderly who are more frail and have less family support, there will be more places in residential care facilities, such as nursing homes, to provide them with the appropriate long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the National Council of Social Service and SG Enable will form a Singapore Together Alliances for Action (AfA) to look into bolstering support for care-givers of persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Ageing and mental health care-givers
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to make more provisions to assist care-givers of age-related mental health cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With our rapidly ageing population, we will also encounter more age-related mental health cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge MOH to make more provisions to assist care-givers of this vulnerable group.

sections.label: Private breast surgeon, SMA president
sections.summary: The speaker is a private breast surgeon, married with three children, and the first female President of the Singapore Medical Association.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am now a private breast surgeon and married with three children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am the first female President of the Singapore Medical Association.

sections.label: Healthcare subsidies and 2021 Budget
sections.summary: The speaker notes differences in healthcare subsidies, welcomes the increased 2021 healthcare Budget for primary care subsidies, and says those who can afford private healthcare should consider paying.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I saw for myself the differences in healthcare subsidies, and I appreciate that every Singaporean has access to affordable and quality healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad to see an increased Budget for healthcare in 2021, to cater for patient subsidies in primary care, namely the three new polyclinics and another restructured hospital, Woodlands Health Campus.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I may be stating the obvious, but healthcare subsidies are finite, and those of us who can afford to pay for private healthcare should consider doing so.

sections.label: Insurer panels and policy changes
sections.summary: The speaker says the restructured healthcare system is robust, urges Integrated Shield Plan holders to track term changes, and lists three insurer issues for Committee of Supply debates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Otherwise, I am confident that our restructured healthcare system is robust and can provide adequate care for all citizens.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Those of us with the financial ability to have bought an Integrated Shield Plan will need to keep up to date with the changes to the terms and conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There have been on-going discussions between various stakeholders on some of these issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I list three main ones for thought, and will further speak on these during the Committee of Supply debates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, is it fair for insurers to make unilateral changes to existing policies that affect policy holders?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, is it restrictive to have panels, keeping in mind that some panels have only one or no doctors in an area of speciality?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three, how do the insurers choose their doctors to sit on their panels – is it truly based on quality and merit, or are there financial arrangements which are not disclosed?

sections.label: Reported cyberbullying incidents remain low

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A previous written response stated that reported cyberbullying incidents remain low over the past three years.

sections.label: Gifts for frontline healthcare workers
sections.summary: Frontline healthcare workers, particularly in restructured hospitals, received gifts and care packages, and the speaker supports the Arts and Cultural Resilience Package.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our frontline healthcare workers, particularly those in the restructured hospitals received gifts and care packages, such as coffee, chicken rice, chocolates, vouchers and thank you cards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support the Government's Arts and Cultural Resilience Package: doctors heal the body, religious leaders heal the soul; the arts heal our spirit.

sections.label: Survey on class segregation
sections.summary: A survey commissioned by Dr Janil Puthucheary found class segregation and class division emerging as Singapore's biggest fault line.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: According to a survey commissioned by my esteemed colleague Dr Janil Puthucheary, class segregation and class division is emerging as the biggest fault line in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: In 2019, there were almost 67,600 people above the age of 65 living alone, with 86% of them wishing to live in the same flats that they raised their families in.

sections.label: Share to Care housing strategy
sections.summary: The speaker proposes elderly homeowners rent spare rooms to low-income families at HDB-subsidised rates, called "Share to Care".

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: At the same time, almost 10% of all rental households have more than four members and many have care-giving needs that cannot be fulfilled by existing care channels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: A simple solution then exists, to encourage more elderly homeowners to share their living space, by renting out their spare rooms to low-income families at appropriate rates subsidised by HDB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Such a housing sharing strategy will help to mitigate class silos and reduce the need to build more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I call this the "Share to Care" strategy.

sections.label: Charity tax deductions and grants
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes extending 250% IPC tax deductions to end 2023 and a $20 million Change for Charity grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: It is a whole sector of people who work in caring for our underserved communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I am very thankful and encouraged by the Budget announcement that the 250% Institute of Public Character, or IPC tax-deductions for donations will be extended to end 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I am also very grateful to the Deputy Prime Minister for initiating the $20 million Change for Charity grant to encourage those who can afford to spend, to spend towards charity.

sections.label: COVID-19 Resilience Package allocations
sections.summary: The Budget allocates $11 billion for structural economic policies in the COVID-19 Resilience Package, with $24 billion more over three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: In the current Budget, $11 billion have been allocated for structural economic policies in the COVID-19 Resilience Package, with another $24 billion committed over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Much of it focuses on equipping businesses and workers for industry transformations and future-ready capabilities.

sections.label: Sharing budget with Careforce
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Deputy Prime Minister to share the $11 billion COVID-19 Resilience Budget with the social services sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: So that we can avoid, in the future, heading down the slippery slope of a welfare state.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I seek the Deputy Prime Minister to share the $11 billion COVID-19 Resilience Budget with our Careforce – the social services sector to make this happen.

sections.label: Singapore Green Plan tree planting
sections.summary: The Singapore Green Plan 2030 targets doubling annual tree planting to plant 1 million more trees and having every household within a 10-minute walk from a park.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the City in Nature element of the Singapore Green Plan 2030, it details that we target to double our annual tree planting rate to plant 1 million more trees across Singapore, while increasing the land area of our nature parks, such that every household will be within 10-minutes’ walk from a park.

sections.label: Mummy's milestone booklet proposal
sections.summary: Proposes a Mummy's milestone booklet for expecting couples to track the mother's development and provide pregnancy information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In light of this, I would therefore like to propose to develop a "Mummy’s milestone booklet", to be provided to expecting couples.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In Taiwan, it is called "the Maternal Health Handbook – 孕妇健康手册".

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This milestone booklet would be akin to a baby's health booklet, but instead would help to track the expecting mother’s physical and emotional development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At the same time, it would also contain pertinent information by health practitioners regarding the necessary preparations for each stage of pregnancy, parenting best practices and as well as a list of the support systems available to all parents for the first few years of their journey into parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Some examples of what I envision would be in the booklet include items such as a checklist of vaccinations required for expecting mothers, recommended dates to sign up for pre-natal classes and a checklist of items to prepare for the arrival of the baby, along with tips on how to spot signs of labour or post-natal depression symptoms, and where to seek support in this regard.

sections.label: Online estate planning portal
sections.summary: Suggests an online estate planning portal with Ministries to educate families on legal matters and contingency planning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Apart from the grief of losing a loved one abruptly, their families will also eventually need to deal with the aftermath, including the issue of finding a new way to secure their livelihood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I humbly suggest that we consider setting up an estate planning portal online, with support from multiple Ministries, to start educating families on essential legal knowledge and encourage them to begin planning for contingencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This portal will be dedicated to administrative matters such as CPF nominations, lodging of Lasting Power of Attorney applications, advance medical directives, as well as the registering of wills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Lastly, the portal can also provide further value by collaborating with the Singapore Academy of Law, to provide bite-sized, easy-to-understand legal knowledge on estate planning and the Law Society's Pro Bono Services to devise a way for the platform to dispense legal advice virtually.

sections.label: CPF nomination figures
sections.summary: States that more than two in five CPF members have made a nomination on who receives their CPF savings after death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At present, more than two in five CPF members have made a nomination on who will receive their CPF savings after their death, as well as the percentage received by each beneficiary.

sections.label: PayNow for funeral expenses
sections.summary: Hopes the Government will consider using PayNow to transfer deceased CPF savings to beneficiaries immediately to defray funeral expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To encourage more CPF members to nominate their beneficiaries, I hope the Government will consider using PayNow to transfer a sum of money from the deceased CPF savings to the nominated beneficiary’s bank account immediately upon his death so as to defray the funeral expenses of the deceased and alleviate the financial burden of the family during this period.

sections.label: Concern over reserves spending
sections.summary: Raises concern over Singapore's fiscal position, noting it is the third time and second consecutive year of dipping into reserves.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, beyond the initial high over these astronomical investments into new growth areas, I cannot help but to be concerned over our current fiscal position and wonder how Singapore is evolving as a nation when it comes to national spending.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is the third time and second consecutive year that we are dipping into our reserves.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Would Deputy Prime Minister Heng be outlining a projected timeline and roadmap on when these amounts would be returned to the reserves?

sections.label: Micro jobs for special needs
sections.summary: Asks whether avenues can be found for more micro jobs for adults with special needs in the new economy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the new and future economy, can we find avenues for more micro jobs to be created for adults with special needs?

sections.label: Part-time work for women
sections.summary: Connecting women to part-time work near home helps essential workers, low-income families and single mothers balance care-giving and supplement income.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Connect the women who can provide part-time services within distance of their home, enable essential workers, especially the low-income families or single mothers to balance care-giving duties and also supplement their income with work within the community.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: A recent example is that of a Ghim Moh resident, Ms Looi, who set up a community library for children at the lift landing in front of her HDB flat.

sections.label: Elderly residents' expiring land lease
sections.summary: In the speaker's constituency, some elderly residents in Chempaka Kuning have land leases expiring in 2034.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: In my own constituency, I have some elderly residents living in Chempaka Kuning area whose land lease expires in 2034, just 13 years from now.

sections.label: Little support due to property assets
sections.summary: They receive little or no Government support because their property assets mean they do not meet qualifying criteria for many handouts.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Each time, they receive little or no Government support as their property assets mean that they do not meet the qualifying criteria for many of the handouts.

sections.label: Rethink annual property value criteria
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to rethink annual property value assessment and means-testing in crises, and consider utilities and transport vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: While I understand the rationale of having a viable economy and healthy employment rate that supports a broad segment of society, but what happens to those who fall through the cracks and are unable to monetise their assets during crisis due to the policies that are in place, health conditions and family complications.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Thus, with these considerations in mind, I would like to ask if the Government can rethink how annual values of properties should be assessed as a criterion, if the applicants actually fulfill all other criteria for each of the benefit schemes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Also, the need for annual property value criteria under means-testing to be differently considered in times of crisis, for example the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider providing support on essentials related to utilities and transport vouchers for this particular group as most are no longer working or have no private transportation means.

sections.label: Budget viewed with strategic importance
sections.summary: The Budget should be viewed with strategic importance, preserving national interests without costing future generations and future relevancy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: As a nation, beyond the immediate handouts that many look forward to in the release of Budgets, it is critical that we view the Budget with a lens of strategic importance – preserving our national strategic interests and standing and ensuring that with immediate problems being addressed, it does not come at the cost of future generations and our future relevancy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is my belief that voluntary egg freezing can be allowed with legislation and a proper framework put in place.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The appeal failed and the couple paid for it on their own.

sections.label: Embryo screening lab requirement

sections.label: Embryo screening pilot programme

sentences.text: We have had a pilot programme for three years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We should allow more to screen their embryos if they have suffered miscarriages, provided no gender selection.

sections.summary: About 210,000 working women have benefited from financial support through these schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: All in all, about 210,000 of our working women have benefited from financial support through these schemes.

sections.label: Taskforce on Family Violence proposals
sections.summary: The Taskforce on the Prevention of Family Violence will put up proposals on awareness, help processes and interventions for perpetrators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Taskforce on the Prevention of Family Violence which I co-chair, will be putting up its proposals to see how we can raise further awareness about family violence and the channels of help available, refine processes to ensure ready and effective help rendered to victims and propose interventions where perpetrators are concerned.

sections.label: Budget 2021 support for women
sections.summary: About 210,000 working women benefited from financial support, and Budget 2021 introduces a Household Support Package and Inclusive Support Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Through the temporary relief fund, the COVID-19 support grant and the recently launched COVID-19 recovery grant, about 210,000 working women in Singapore have benefited from financial support in these difficult times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: And as announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng in the Budget Statement, we will be introducing a Household Support Package and lower to middle income families will receive more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This will also benefit elderly females who live alone, and therefore have fewer means and family support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For women with children or who are care-givers, they will also benefit from increased support via the Inclusive Support Programme which provides in-school support to children with up to medium level developmental needs and seeks to lessen care-giving burden.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Budget 2021 builds on past efforts to support women and their families and we hope we can work with all parties to build an equitable and inclusive society, where women are supported and enabled to achieve their fullest potential.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers Tranche 2
sections.summary: After a first $20 million tranche, the CDCs rolled out another $20 million of CDC Vouchers in January, with over 7,000 merchants participating.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The first tranche of $20 million was rolled out last year to lower and middle income households, to much success.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With that good support, the CDCs recently rolled out another $20 million of CDC Vouchers – what we called Tranche 2 – in January this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: More than 7,000 merchants have participated in the scheme and there was good feedback.

sections.label: Vouchers extended to all households
sections.summary: The tranche is more than seven times the initial two exercises because the vouchers were extended to every Singaporean household.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The tranche is now more than seven times the initial two exercises – due to one key reason.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng and his team had listened and decided that the vouchers would be extended to every Singaporean household, regardless of public or private dwelling.

sections.label: Online reach and SkillsFuture workshops
sections.summary: In one week last year, partners reached over 250,000 viewers online and more than 6,000 joined online SkillsFuture workshops.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In fact, in one week last year, the partners managed to reach out and connect over 250,000 viewers online and more than 6,000 of them joined in the online SkillsFuture workshops.

sections.label: CDC local district initiatives
sections.summary: Between February and October 2020, the five CDCs rolled out close to 70 local district initiatives serving over 676,000 beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With these networks, the five CDCs were able to quickly roll out, during the pandemic between February and October 2020, close to 70 local district initiatives that served over 676,000 beneficiaries.

sections.label: CDC fundraising amount
sections.summary: The CDCs raised $12.3 million in cash and kind last year through their networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Last year, the CDCs drew on their networks to raise $12.3 million, in cash and kind.

sections.label: Signature district CDC programmes
sections.summary: The passage names signature CDC programmes, including Club 100, WALK FOR RICE, ADOPT @ South West, Project Refresh, Ready for School Cheques, Digital Bootcamps and The Purple Parade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Some of the more signature district programmes include – let me name just a few on behalf of my fellow Mayors: (a) North West CDC’s Club 100 which has close to 800 regular donors collectively contributing $1 million a year towards the Northwest Food Aid Programme which benefits low-income households in their 19 divisions; (b) South East CDC’s famous WALK FOR RICE @ South East in which rice and oats are donated to the district’s vulnerable families, for every 300 metres that participants walk or run; (c) South West – under Ms Low Yen Ling – South West CDC’s ADOPT @ South West leads more than 100 corporate and community partners to uplift the vulnerable in social wellness, healthcare, home safety, education and enrichment; (d) North East CDC’s Project Refresh, led by Mayor Desmond Choo, which supports more than 10 volunteer agencies and have refurbished close to 400 households; activating close to 3,500 corporate volunteers; (e) For Central Singapore district, my CDC, with which, of course, I am most familiar – there are 52 actually in the suite of programmes we have – let me name a few: (a) Ready for School Cheques, vouchers donated by Far East Organisation to relieve cost of starting school for 12,000 students in the rental households; (b) The holiday Digital Bootcamps sponsored by UOB for 2,000 students so they would not be overly affected or left behind by any digital divide; (c) Pan-district projects like The Purple Parade – and I thank Members of Parliament who have joined in this Parade – which is supported by all five Mayors and CDCs.

sections.label: The Purple Parade participation
sections.summary: The Purple Parade reached over 10,000 participants annually and connected over 200 corporate and community partners each year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Purple Parade reached out to over 10,000 participants annually and connected over 200 corporate and community partners – MNCs like Apple, HP and so forth, local Statutory Boards like the Building Construction Authority (BCA), LTA, MSF, MOE, SMEs, large local enterprises, schools and more than 40 disability organisations – every year.

sections.label: Response to Pritam Singh accusation
sections.summary: The passage rejects Mr Pritam Singh's accusation about CDC vouchers and asks whether he accepted the Leader of the Opposition role to be relevant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh's accusation that the Government is trying to find some way for the CDCs to be relevant by asking them to manage the CDC vouchers scheme, is belittling the CDCs and their partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: When Prime Minister Lee graciously created the role of the Leader of the Opposition, much to the surprise of Mr Singh himself, did Mr Singh not accept the role when asked, and the office and the research assistant and the salary and try to do his best to be relevant too?

sections.label: CDC public mindshare comment
sections.summary: The comment on the CDCs' relative absence in public mindshare prompted thought, and the biggest mistake may have been not publicising their work better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: His comment on the CDCs' "relative absence" in the public mindshare has also given us some food for thought.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the biggest mistake the CDCs made was not to have better publicised the work we do.

sections.label: Avoid politicising CDC work
sections.summary: The passage states the real work is in the work and people benefited, and hopes the CDCs' and partners' good work is not politicised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The real work is in the work and the people we benefited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I hope that there are no attempts to politicise the good work of the CDCs and especially our partners.

sections.label: Mayors part-time then full-time
sections.summary: CDCs' Mayors were part-time when formed in 1996/1997 and became full-time appointments after the 2001 General Elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When the CDCs were first formed in 1996/1997, the Mayors were not full-time; they were part-time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They became full-time appointments, to my understanding, after the General Elections in 2001.

sections.label: CDC budget increase 1997 to 2001
sections.summary: The CDCs' budget rose from $19 million in 1997 to $153 million in 2001.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The budget of the CDCs was increased from $19 million in 1997 to $153 million in 2001.

sections.label: Full-time Mayors viability and pay
sections.summary: A Member asks if full-time Mayors remain viable; the speaker says he is probably the only full-time Mayor and fellow Mayors get one pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I think the question which the hon Member Ms Denise Phua did not answer is: is it still viable for Mayors to be full-time?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I have to say that I am probably the only full-time Mayor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: My fellow Mayors are all double hatting or triple hatting sometimes; and so I do not know whether you consider them full-time Mayors or not.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: But I do know that they only get one pay.

sections.label: Petrol duties and GST squeeze
sections.summary: The increase in petrol duties adds to the squeeze, as will the future hike in GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The increase in petrol duties adds to this squeeze and so will the future hike in GST.

sections.label: Flexibility in assessing assistance eligibility
sections.summary: Assistance should stay targeted but eligibility assessment should be more flexible, so applicants narrowly missing requirements or with special circumstances are not denied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Assistance should still be targeted but I hope to see more flexibility when it comes to assessing the eligibility of applicants for schemes, like the COVID-19 Recovery Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Individuals who narrowly miss eligibility requirements or have circumstances that deserve special consideration should not be denied assistance.

sections.label: OECD automation job figures
sections.summary: According to the OECD, 14% of jobs in rich countries are highly automatable and a further 32% are likely to change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the OECD, 14% of jobs in rich countries are highly automatable while the further a 32% are likely to change because of because many of their routine tasks can be automated.

sections.label: Recognition for workers
sections.summary: The passage calls for sufficient recognition of workers in positions such as repairmen, refuse collectors and delivery drivers, while noting nurses and healthcare workers are getting a raise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We need to accord sufficient recognition to workers manning these positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am glad that nurses and healthcare workers are getting a much-deserved raise, but let us not forget our repairmen, refuse collectors and delivery drivers.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model coverage
sections.summary: The 2012 Progressive Wage Model still covers only 15% of the lowest income quintile and three sectors, with 100,000 workers elsewhere earning under $1,300 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2012, the Government introduced the Progressive Wage Model, or PWM, to raise the wages of low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, almost a decade later, the PWM still covers only 15% of workers in the lowest quintile of income earners and only from three industry sectors: security, cleaning and landscaping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to MOM, there are a residual 100,000 workers in other sectors who still earn less than $1,300 a month.

sections.label: Elderly household budget study
sections.summary: A 2019 NTU and NUS study found a single elderly household needs $1,379 monthly and an elderly couple $2,351 monthly for basic living standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A household budget study by researchers from NTU and NUS in 2019, found that to meet basic standards of living in Singapore, a single elderly household needs $1,379 per month while an elderly couple needs $2,351 per month.

sections.label: PWM rollout to more sectors
sections.summary: NTUC Deputy Secretary-General Koh Poh Koon shared plans to roll out the PWM to six more sectors in the next two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: NTUC Deputy Secretary-General Koh Poh Koon shared plans to roll out the PWM to six more sectors in the next two to three years.

sections.label: Pace of PWM rollout
sections.summary: The passage states the current pace of PWM rollout is much too slow and it will take another decade or more for all low-wage workers to be covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The current pace of rollout of the PWM is much too slow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At this rate, it will be another decade or more before all low-wage workers are on the PWM.

sections.label: Implementing minimum wage portion
sections.summary: The passage urges focusing on implementing the minimum wage portion of the PWM across all sectors first, using Workfare Income Supplement to top up wages temporarily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given the urgency of the problem that remains to be addressed – 100,000 employed and self-employed workers earning less than $1,300 a month – we need to pick our battles more carefully and focus on what will move the needle the most and the quickest for our low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since the PWM is a "minimum wage plus", we should focus on implementing the "minimum wage" portion of the PWM across all industry sectors as soon as possible, then roll out the "plus" portion only later where practical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To ease the transition for all employers, the Workfare Income Supplement can be used to temporarily top up wages to the minimum wage, and these can be eased off as the economy recovers, with employers taking over.

sections.label: Senior worker grants and funding
sections.summary: Over $200 million goes to Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and Part-Time Re-employment Grant, with more funding to redesign jobs and senior-friendly workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: More than $200 million will be allocated for the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and the Part-Time Re-employment Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There will be increased funding to redesign jobs and leverage on technology to develop senior-friendly workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This comes on top of the raising of the Retirement Age and Re-employment Age to 63 and 69 respectively from July 2022.

sections.label: Work permit holder quarantine
sections.summary: Newly arrived work permit and S Pass holders must complete a 14-Day Stay-Home Notice, quarantined for as many as 21 days in total.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Newly arrived work permit and S Pass holders are required to complete a 14-Day Stay-Home Notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In total, they will be quarantined for as many as 21 days.

sections.label: Temporary Living Quarters expiry
sections.summary: The Temporary Living Quarters scheme is slated to expire at the end of March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Temporary Living Quarters scheme is slated to expire in end March 2021.

sections.label: COVID-19 Act cost co-sharing
sections.summary: The COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act introduced co-sharing of project prolongation costs for public sector construction contracts, and asks how many claims were made and processed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act introduced co-sharing of project prolongation costs for public sector construction contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How many claims were made, and how many have been processed?

sections.label: Preference for local businesses
sections.summary: Studies show that giving preference to local businesses can benefit the country's finances as a whole, even if the project costs a little more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Yet studies have shown that giving preference to local businesses can benefit the country's finances as a whole, even if it means spending a little more on the project itself.

sections.label: Expansionary infrastructure approach
sections.summary: The Government should consider an expansionary approach and press ahead with pipeline infrastructure projects rather than defer them, as the economy and employment rate show recovery signs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Rather than defer infrastructure projects, the Government should consider taking an expansionary approach, and press ahead with projects in the pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One year on, the economy and employment rate are showing signs of recovery.

sections.label: PWM in strata and solar
sections.summary: He asked why the Labour Movement pushes for a PWM in strata management and the solar technology sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The first thing he asked was why we push for a PWM in strata management as well as solar technology sector.

sections.label: Wage stagnation and PWM rationale
sections.summary: Wage stagnation from contract renewals and no career progression explains the push for PWM, which was never meant only for low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Many of them have seen wage stagnation because as each contract is renewed, there is some resetting of their wages and there is no career progression, even though in terms of absolute pay, it may not be at the lowest bottom end of the bottom 20.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: So, that is the reason why we are pushing for that.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: And in essence from the first, when the Labour Movement first talk about PWM in 2012, actually the PWM construct, while is tightly linked to low wage workers, it was never construed as only for low-wage workers, because the whole idea of the four-wage ladders – wage tied to skills to productivity and career progression is applied to all jobs or job roles across the different parts of the industries.

sections.label: Tripartite workgroup discussion focus
sections.summary: This is a focus of the tripartite workgroup's discussion, with hope for implementation without agencies holding a similar regulatory lever.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: I think that is a focus of the tripartite workgroup's discussion and we hope that we can land on something that can allow us to implement this, without the necessary agencies that may have a particular regulatory lever similar to other sectors that were implemented in the past.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: And hopefully, this can be a recommendation from the work group sometime in the later part of the year.

sections.label: Minimum wage warning
sections.summary: The Labour Movement says that in pushing for too high a minimum wage, a minimum wage can become no wage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement always keeps saying this: that in pushing for too high a minimum wage, a minimum wage can become no wage.

sections.label: Covering low-wage workers first
sections.summary: He shares concerns about wage stagnation but asks why not focus first on covering all 100,000 low-wage workers not covered by the PWM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I share his concerns about wage stagnation in any sector, not just the low-wage sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: But my point was that, as important as it is to address the wage stagnation issue and provide career ladders for the different industries, why can we not just focus more first on the low-wage workers to ensure that all 100,000 low-wage workers who are not covered by the PWM now, are covered first.

sections.label: PWM and unemployment question
sections.summary: He asks whether cleaning, security and landscaping saw massive unemployment from the PWM, and doubts a reasonable $1,300 wage floor would cause it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: In the cleaning sector, the security sector and in landscaping, have we seen massive unemployment is the result of the implementation of the PWM?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: And I believe that if we implement a wage floor which is reasonable, and we have actually put out a number there – $1,300 a month – if we implement a wage floor which is reasonable, I do not think we will see massive unemployment.

sections.label: Sectoral PWM minimum wage floor
sections.summary: The minimum wage floor in a PWM is not standalone because a Workfare Income Supplement top-up brings salaries beyond $1,300, closer to $2,000 or $2,300.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Or are you going with me now on my sectoral PWM with a minimum wage floor, sectorally?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But I think what the Member must also remember in my previous Parliamentary speech on this topic, is that the minimum wage floor in a PWM is not a standalone because there is a Government top-up with a Workfare Income Supplement that brings the salary way beyond $1,300.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In fact, most of them will hit closer to $2,000 or $2,300.

sections.label: Minimum wage for low-wage workers
