sections.summary: The position remains that a minimum wage should be rolled out first to all low-wage workers earning less than $1,300 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Our position still remains that we should roll out a minimum wage first, to all low-wage workers who earn less than $1,300 a month.

sections.label: Sectoral wage floors and disemployment
sections.summary: Sectoral wage floors aim to keep the minimum wage floor relevant to the industry, job, and what industry and consumers can bear, avoiding disemployment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: When we talk about sectoral wage floors, we are trying to make sure that the minimum wage floor by the sector is relevant to the particular industry, that job, and what the industry can bear, what the consumers are prepared to pay for the type of services so that that particular wage floor for the sector does not cause disemployment or unemployment in the sector.

sections.label: Occupational PWMs and sectoral wage floor
sections.summary: The strategy is to push vocational PWMs covering different job types and the bottom 20% of earners, with a tripartite work group expected to recommend occupational PWMs by year-end.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It is a little bit more laborious maybe, but that makes sure that it is something the industry, businesses and consumers are prepared to bear.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I said yesterday that we are looking at the option of pushing up for vocational PWM so that it actually involves different job types, especially those in the bottom 20% of income earners across multiple sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That is our strategy – we hope to cover as many of the low-hanging fruits and those who are in need, as the Member was pointing out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I hope by the end of this year, the tripartite work group will be able to come up with recommendations to push out occupational PWMs to cover the most vulnerable who are currently not covered by the mandatory PWM, sectorally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Just the last point on the sectoral wage floor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: We want to see a $1,300 minimum wage across all sectors eventually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: As for the sectoral wage floor, we acknowledge that one way of rolling out this $1,300 is to implement $1,300 wage floor for each sector, going sector by sector.

sections.label: Singapore Teachers' Union survey
sections.summary: The Singapore Teachers' Union surveyed about 1,200 teachers and held closed-door dialogues with teachers of all levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Singapore Teachers' Union surveyed about 1,200 teachers and organised a series of closed-door dialogues with teachers of all levels who spoke candidly about their experiences.

sections.label: Teacher appraisal system concerns
sections.summary: Over 80% of teachers and 70% of Reporting Officers agreed that ranking is not the best way to appraise all job holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Large numbers of them expressed concerns about their appraisal system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Over 80% of teachers and 70% of Reporting Officers, or ROs, agreed that ranking is not the best way to appraise all job holders.

sections.label: Standardising teacher appraisal process
sections.summary: The speaker proposes standardising the appraisal process and requiring schools to follow it, citing teacher survey support for standardised criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first proposal is to standardise the appraisal process and require schools to follow it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While about half of the teachers surveyed felt there was some objectivity in the system, about three quarters of teachers surveyed agreed that appraisals should be based on standardised criteria.

sections.label: Ranking Panel unequal say
sections.summary: More than half of the ROs said that members of the Ranking Panel have an unequal say.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: More than half of the ROs said that members of the Ranking Panel have an unequal say.

sections.label: Teacher views on ranking transparency
sections.summary: About three quarters of teachers surveyed agreed appraisals should use standardised criteria, and almost 80% did not feel the ranking process was made transparent to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Again, about three quarters of teachers surveyed agreed that appraisals should be based on standardised criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Almost 80% of teachers surveyed did not feel that the process of ranking has been made transparent them.

sections.label: Removing grade quota proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes removing the quota for each grade, and close to 80% of teachers surveyed strongly agreed with this proposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, I propose that we remove the quota for each grade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Close to 80% of teachers surveyed strongly agreed with this proposal.

sections.label: Compulsory low grade quota
sections.summary: Five percent of each school's teachers must be graded C-, D or E.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Five percent of each school’s teachers must be graded C-, D or E.

sections.label: Consequences of C- grades
sections.summary: MOE says the C- grade is not adverse, but recipients of C- and below face punitive measures including three-year promotion ineligibility and ineligibility for Professional Development Leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Indeed, MOE has said the C- grade is not an adverse grade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But the reality is that those receiving C- grades and below, face a host of punitive measures, including ineligibility for promotion for three years and ineligibility for Professional Development Leave.

sections.label: Teacher support for quota removal
sections.summary: Over 80% of teachers surveyed supported removing the quota.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Over 80% of teachers surveyed supported the removal of the quota.

sections.label: General Electric and C-grade measures
sections.summary: General Electric shifted to continuous dialogue and shared accountability, and 75% of teachers surveyed agreed to remove punitive measures for the C-grade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: General Electric has shifted to a system that emphasises continuous dialogue and shared accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also propose that we remove the punitive measures for the C- grade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Seventy-five percent of teachers surveyed agreed with this.

sections.label: Educator calls for balanced performance model
sections.summary: An educator calls for the Public Service to tweak the ranking exercise and move towards a balanced model of performance and development.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As an educator, I believe that it is important that we continue to recognise our top performers but I also believe that those who did not do well, for whatever reasons, be given a chance to bounce back and emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I call for the Public Service to lead the way in tweaking the ranking exercise and move towards a balanced model of performance and development.

sections.label: Four strategies for mental health
sections.summary: The speaker calls for four strategies: mental health and digital literacy in schools, accessible touchpoints, mental health screening, and workplace and school time-outs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We need to make concrete and concerted efforts to support those with mental health issues beyond mere awareness and promote positive mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I call again for these four strategies: first, to enhance mental health literacy as well as digital literacy programmes in our schools; second, to create more accessible touchpoints so that those who feel that they need help are able to do easily; third, including mental health screening as part of physical health screening and this should not be limited to just schools or workplaces only but also within the community so that our seniors may also receive help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Lastly, to introduce time-outs at workplaces and in schools, so that those who are under stress may take the option to take a mental break, but such breaks are recorded and the next time one takes it, we know that they may have something that we need to help with.

sections.label: Broad skills and education pathways
sections.summary: The speaker calls for MOE to review pathways for graduates' agility and to ease progression from Secondary school to ITEs or Polytechnics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I emphasised the need for broad skills that can be generalised across other disciplines so that we can put our fresh graduates on a better footing and give them the confidence to apply their technical skills across other relevant sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I call for MOE to continuously review pathways, to prepare our graduates with the agility to navigate through the varied and diversified workforce and discover their passion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I also call to review how we can ease the progression from Secondary school to ITEs or the Polytechnics so that anyone who has a passion for a certain field, are allowed to seize it.

sections.label: Increase in abuse and harassment cases
sections.summary: Abuse and harassment cases rose from 1,080 in 2018 to 1,300 last year, with police-reported cases involving on-duty public healthcare workers rising from 40 to 58.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The number of abuse and harassment cases increased from 1,080 in 2018 to 1,300 last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Over the same period, the number of such cases involving on duty public healthcare workers that were reported to the Police under the Protection of Harassment Act increased from 40 to 58.

sections.label: Mental health school and workplace measures
sections.summary: Proposals include compulsory mental health education and digital literacy in schools, mental health screening in physical health checks, and time-out for stressed students and workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, make mental health education and digital literacy programmes compulsory in schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Third, introduce mental health screening in the current physical health checks, and lastly, introduce "time-out" for students and workers who are suffering from stress or mental issues.

sections.label: Healthcare workers' salaries increase
sections.summary: The passage thanks healthcare workers for their sacrifices and welcomes the Budget plan to increase their salaries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We thank them for their sacrifices and hard work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I welcome the plan to increase the salaries of workers in the healthcare sectors as stated in this Budget.

sections.label: Singapore mental health study findings
sections.summary: The 2016 study found one in seven had a mood, anxiety or alcohol use disorder, up from one in eight in 2010, with youth more vulnerable and 78% not seeking help.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The 2016 Singapore Mental Health study found that one in seven persons "has experienced a mood, anxiety or alcohol user disorder in his or her lifetime." This was a marked increase from the same study conducted in 2010, where one in eight persons was found to have suffered from some form of mental disorder.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Also, noteworthy in the 2016 study was the finding that young people stood out as a demographic group more vulnerable to mental disorders.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: And the same survey also found that a large majority, in fact, 78% of people with mental illness did not seek help.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As many as seven in 10 think that persons with mental health conditions experience discrimination in their daily lives, according to the 2017 NCSS study on attitudes towards persons with mental health conditions in Singapore.

sections.label: Inclusive Support Programme pilot
sections.summary: Many applaud the Inclusive Support Programme pilot, which provides integrated early intervention and early childhood services to help children with developmental needs upstream.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Many of them applaud the Inclusive Support Programme pilot, which will see the integrated provision of early intervention and early childhood services, so that we can better help children with developmental needs upstream.

sections.label: School fees for autistic students
sections.summary: Monthly fees are $25 for a Singapore Citizen in a mainstream MOE secondary school, $250 at Pathlight School, and were $500 for Amelia some years back.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The monthly fees for a Singapore Citizen to receive an education in a mainstream MOE Secondary school is $25.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In contrast, the monthly fee for an autistic student at the Pathlight School is $250.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: When Amelia was going through school some years back, her monthly fee at Pathlight then, at that time, was $500.

sections.label: Employment of persons with disabilities
sections.summary: According to MOM, 28.6% of resident persons with disabilities aged 15 to 64 are employed and another 4.2% are active job seekers.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: According to MOM, 28.6% of resident persons with disabilities aged 15 to 64 are employed, while another 4.2% are active job seekers.

sections.label: President's Challenge inclusive hiring
sections.summary: 64 organisations were lauded at the President's Challenge for their inclusive hiring practices last year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Last year, I understand that 64 organisations were lauded at the President's Challenge for their inclusive hiring practices.

sections.label: Sector share of GDP
sections.summary: The sector accounts for about 21%, or $106 billion, of total gross domestic product.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The sector currently accounts for about 21%, or $106 billion of our total gross domestic product.

sections.label: Smart manufacturing and manufacturing growth
sections.summary: Smart manufacturing is expected to be worth $220.4 billion by 2025, and the Government plans to grow manufacturing by 50% over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Post-COVID-19, smart manufacturing is expected to be worth $220.4 billion by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government plans to grow our manufacturing sector by 50% over the next 10 years.

sections.label: CTP extension beneficiaries
sections.summary: With the CTP extension in this Budget, over 970 locals and more than 140 companies are projected to benefit from 40 projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the extension of the CTP in this Budget, it has been projected that over 970 locals and more than 140 companies will benefit from 40 projects.

sections.label: Petrol duty hike
sections.summary: A Budget petrol duty hike will increase petrol by 10-15 cents per litre, though the impact on inflation is still minimal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With a hike in petrol duty announced during the Budget, there will be an increase of 10-15 cents per litre even though the impact on inflation is still minimal.

sections.label: Road tax rebates
sections.summary: The Government is giving private car owners a 15% road tax rebate for one year and motorcycle owners 60%, plus additional offsets for those who use vehicles to earn a living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To ease the transition, the Government is giving a 15% road tax rebate to owners of private cars for one year, while motorcycle owners will get 60% road tax rebate For those who use their vehicles to earn a living, the Government has provided additional offsets to ease the transition.

sections.label: Electric motorcycles in Singapore
sections.summary: Rules on electric motorcycles were relaxed, but only two were registered as of March 2020 out of over 140,000 motorcycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Last year, Government relaxed rules on electric motorcycles, allowing high-powered motorbikes on the roads as part of efforts to encourage usage of cleaner vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But as of March 2020, there are only two electric motorcycles registered in Singapore, out of a total motorcycle population of more than 140,000.

sections.label: Norway EV tax incentive
sections.summary: Norway removed its 25% sales tax on new EV purchases in 2001 to incentivise EV ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Norway, which is known for being world leader on EV penetration and sales rate, the government incentivised EV ownership by removing their 25% sales tax from new EV purchases in 2001.

sections.label: Reserves data and speculators
sections.summary: Publicising reserves data is likened to revealing ammunition size to hedge funds and speculators, with risks outweighing transparency benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I do not think we want to add the additional element of this risk into the equation for our Singaporean job seekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, publicising data from our reserves is akin to revealing the size of our ammunition to hedge funds and speculators out there with large pool of funds to play with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The potential risks and downsides outweigh the benefits of transparency.

sections.label: Norway and Singapore policy differences
sections.summary: Norway uses an interest rate and free-floating currency, unlike Singapore's exchange rate, and has a different economy and VAT rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Norway's policy rate is the interest rate on banks' overnight deposit rates in Norges Bank and its currency is free floating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Now, remember, I mentioned earlier, Singapore uses its exchange rate, not its interest rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Norway, its petrol-driven economy is also very different from ours and with a value-added tax or VAT of up to 25%, it is in stark contrast to our GST rate.

sections.label: Temasek, MAS, GIC fund sizes
sections.summary: Temasek and MAS fund sizes are made public, while only GIC's is not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, Temasek and MAS fund sizes are made public, only GIC’s is not.

sections.label: 50-50 divide explained in 2008
sections.summary: The Prime Minister explained the current 50 to 50 percentage divide when the framework was introduced in 2008.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The current 50 to 50 percentage divide was explained by the Prime Minister when the framework was first introduced in 2008.

sections.label: Fundamental exchange rate and speculation
sections.summary: The passage states that being off fundamentally determined exchange rates could encourage speculation to return to the fundamental rate, a point argued by BBC inventor John Williamson and subscribed to by MAS.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: If we were off our fundamentally determined exchange rates, we could encourage market participants to actually engage in speculative activity that would get us back onto our fundamental exchange rate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This, in fact, was a point that was routinely argued by the inventor of the Basket, Band, Crawl (BBC) system, John Williamson for which we, MAS, subscribes to.

sections.label: Currency attacks during Asian Financial Crisis
sections.summary: The passage states currency attacks can never be stabilising, and during the Asian Financial Crisis attacked currencies like Thailand's depreciated greatly, causing cascading economic effects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The impact of the currency attacks can never be stabilising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: But back in the Asian Financial Crisis, the impact on the currencies that were specifically attacked, like Thailand and even to some extent, other countries in the ASEAN region, was very significant; to the point that the currencies depreciated so much that it led to the ramifications and cascading effects on the economy.

sections.label: Singapore exchange rate versus Norway policy rate
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's reliance on the exchange rate as a controllable intermediate target is distinct from Norway, which uses a policy rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The reliance of using exchange rate as a controllable intermediate target in the Singapore economy is very distinct from Norway which uses a policy rate in its central bank.

sections.label: Exchange rate target and MAS reserves
sections.summary: The passage states Norway uses a policy rate and freely floated exchange rate, while Singapore's exchange rate target affects its ability to intervene and run down MAS reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: If you look at Norway, Norway uses policy rate and its exchange rate is freely floated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: So, for Singapore's case, the very fact that we target, the intermediate target of an exchange rate has some impact in terms of our ability to directly intervene in the markets and thus run down on our reserves, on MAS reserves.

sections.label: Plea to make vaccination mandatory
sections.summary: The passage makes a plea to take a bold step and make vaccination mandatory, citing compulsory pandemic measures, low adverse reactions, and over 216 million people worldwide having received at least a first dose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My first plea this evening is that amidst the boldness of this Budget that looks beyond the now and focuses on the future, post-pandemic, ready not just to take off, but also be at the front of the pack, that we take another bold step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And that suggestion is to make vaccination mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have taken bold steps to control the pandemic over the course of the last one year, many of which involved making things compulsory – mask wearing, social distancing, amongst others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We now have in our hands a weapon that brings the fight to the virus and over 216 million people worldwide have received at least the first dose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Adverse reactions have been very, very low, much like many other common vaccines that we take on a regular basis, and much less risk compared to smoking.

sections.label: Conditional opt-out vaccination and reserves
sections.summary: The passage argues vaccination should be conditionally opt-out rather than voluntarily opt-in, and notes reserves have been drawn on in the last two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If we believe in it, that it works, we should stand by it and, therefore, it should be conditionally opt-out rather than voluntarily opt-in, because only when we control this enemy, this virus, can the bold moves that this Budget and its intents bear fruit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On the topic of fruits, I now move to the kitchen larder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have been drawing from our reserves in the last two years – difficult, but needed decisions.

sections.label: GST buffers and voucher fund
sections.summary: GST has buffers for the low-income, and the GST Voucher Fund Act was passed in March 2020 to cushion GST increases for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: With GST, we have also built in buffers for the low-income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Over and above that, as the hon Member Mr Saktiandi pointed out earlier, we also the GST Voucher Fund Act in March 2020, just under a year ago to cushion the impact of any GST increases for all Singaporeans both low-income and middle income families.

sections.label: Bloomberg on GST and Hong Kong
sections.summary: Andy Mukherjee said Singapore's GST increase funds recurring revenue for permanent costs like healthcare, unlike Hong Kong, which lacks a sales tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Andy Mukherjee of Bloomberg raised the point that Singapore's plan for an increase in GST is to ensure that we have enough recurring revenue to pay for permanent costs, such as healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: He compares these to Hong Kong and says, like Singapore, Hong Kong also has an ageing population, but they do not have a sales tax and has only been able to overcome its lack of steady revenue by fanning a gigantic real estate bubble.

sections.label: GST increase unpopular but necessary
sections.summary: The Government says a GST increase is unpopular but necessary, as a responsible government must do the right thing even if unpopular.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: The Government is cognisant also of the fact that a policy like an increase in GST is unpopular but necessary because, ultimately, the responsibility of a responsible government is to do the right thing, even if occasionally unpopular.

sections.label: Budget expands ComLink programme
sections.summary: This year's Budget lets MSF expand the ComLink programme for low-income families with children from 1,000 to 14,000 families in two years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I also wish to thank our Deputy Prime Minister, as well as the Ministries and agencies which have worked tirelessly behind the scenes all through the Chinese New Year holidays to put forward this year’s Budget.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This year’s Budget allows for MSF to expand the Community Link, or ComLink programme, designed to support low-income families with children, from the current 1,000 families to 14,000 in the next two years.

sections.label: Telok Blangah welfare fund bursaries
sections.summary: Last month the Telok Blangah Community Development Welfare Fund awarded bursaries to 188 children across 118 households from K2 to pre-tertiary.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last month, the Telok Blangah Community Development Welfare Fund awarded bursaries to 188 children across 118 households ranging from K2 to pre-tertiary students.

sections.label: Long-term mentorship reduces recidivism
sections.summary: Among multi-fold interventions to reduce offences and recidivism, long-term mentorship consistent for at least a year has proven most effective.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our interventions to reduce offences and their recidivism rates are multi-fold, but one specific intervention has proven to be most effective in turning lives around, that is, long-term mentorship, mentorship that is consistent for at least a year.

sections.label: Mentoring and savings for disadvantaged youth
sections.summary: The speaker urges long-term mentoring for disadvantaged youth and automatic enrolment of low-income children in the National School Savings Campaign.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Such intervention takes time as these beliefs are often deep-seated.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am fully persuaded that lasting, sustainable change for our disadvantaged young will take place if we invest in long-term mentoring programmes for them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: My hope is that, through ComLink, long-term mentoring will be of easy access for our 10- to 16-year-olds to effect mindset growth and a healthier worldview.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2015, POSB re-introduced the “National School Savings Campaign” to great response and participation by schools.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This programme currently requires the parents to set up the bank account for their children and to monitor it.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I wish to raise for MSF’s consideration the possibility of making enrolment to this programme automatic for our children in low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This will also see to creating a corresponding personal savings account for them, ideally complemented by other initiatives to encourage saving.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Facilitating the process or simplifying it will be of great value to the already time-stretched parents.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This will jumpstart our children in the positive habits of saving and grow a sense of self-efficacy for a fruitful life.

sections.label: Support for the Budget
sections.summary: The speaker affirms support for the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: On this note, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I affirm my support for the Budget.

sections.label: Escalating healthcare operating expenditure
sections.summary: Health operating expenditure is estimated at $17.4 billion this year, making healthcare the highest Head of Expenditure in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Indeed, healthcare costs for us, as a society, are escalating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This year, the operating expenditure for health is estimated to be $17.4 billion, compared to an estimated $11.7 billion last year, and $10 billion in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This makes healthcare the highest Head of Expenditure in 2021, compared to third highest in previous years, after Defence and Education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: A big reason for this is our on-going fight against COVID-19, with close to $5 billion allocated to the COVID-19 Package.

sections.label: Additional healthcare funding allocations
sections.summary: $0.5 billion more has been set aside for patient subsidies, facilities, manpower, MediShield Life premium support and other assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For this year, already, $0.5 billion more has been set aside – for more patient subsidies as three polyclinics open, for the ramp-up of Woodlands Campus, for recruitment of manpower into these new facilities, and for MediShield Life premium support, as well as other forms of grants and financial assistance to Singaporeans.

sections.label: Projected tax and returns growth
sections.summary: The Government projects GST collections recovering 14.6%, corporate income tax growing 8% versus 2019, and Net Investment Returns Contribution up 7.8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: On this note, I like to ask: the Government projects that GST collections this year would recover 14.6% from last year, to roughly 2019 levels, and corporate income tax would grow 8% compared to 2019 before COVID-19, and even Net Investment Returns Contribution would go up 7.8% from last year.

sections.label: Prudence over healthcare subsidy growth
sections.summary: The speaker says healthcare subsidy growth must be prudent because if costs outpace fiscal revenue, redistribution may be needed as the pie is finite.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, we must be very prudent about how much our total outlay in healthcare subsidies should grow in the years ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Now, if costs grow faster than fiscal revenue, then healthcare subsidies might need redistribution because, ultimately, the pie is finite.

sections.label: Early childhood and ComLink support
sections.summary: The speaker supports funding for ECDA, expanding KidSTART, and growing ComLink from 1,000 to 14,000 families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I support the Government’s commitment to intervene actively and intervene more in early life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I support the additional $0.2 billion set aside for the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA), to further develop quality and affordable childcare for every Singaporean child, and I especially look forward to the expansion of KidSTART, so that more children at the bottom can get a holistic and sustained uplift, starting from early in life, even before birth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: There is a whole range of needs – housing, jobs, food, physical and mental health – with complex interdependencies, and we need to coordinate more to address these needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I strongly support the planned expansion of Community Link (ComLink), from 1,000 families in the pilot phase, to 14,000 families, and, hopefully, to many thousands more eventually.

sections.label: Raising healthcare worker salaries
sections.summary: The speaker fully supports raising the salaries of nurses and other healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the area of healthcare, I fully support the move to raise the salaries of nurses and other healthcare workers.

sections.label: Paying more for low-wage workers
sections.summary: The speaker urges society, as consumers, to pay fairer rates for low-wage workers' services, alongside the expanded Progressive Wage Model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: To this end, I agree that the expanded Progressive Wage Model (PWM), when conditions allow, would be a key plank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But at the same time, a big part of the basic equation here, I think, must simply be for all of us to recognise and pay more for low-wage workers' services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is such a stark paradox, but one that bears constant reminding that as the world went into lockdown last year, and as we entered our own circuit breaker, the workers that continued going to work, the workers that could not work from home, the workers that basically kept our world going were so often the low-wage workers providing essential services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, as a society, I think it is high time – high time as COVID-19 rages on – that, we, not the Government, but we – as consumers, as a people – do what is right, what is just, and show our willingness to pay a fairer level for our low-wage workers' services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have an opportunity to shape the post-COVID-19 society that we want to be, transform our compact, transform how we commit to caring for one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has fundamentally upended how we value things in life, reshuffled what truly matters, and redefined how we look at the world, each other, and ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: We can – we must – ride on COVID-19 to emerge as a society that is ever more vested in one another's success, where those with more are ever more willing to put in their treasures, talent and time for those with less, where the hallmark of success is to pay it forward, and to help others do well and be well.

sections.label: Frightening environmental loss figures
sections.summary: The passage cites 15 billion trees cut yearly, over half of rainforests gone, dying coral reefs, and 60% of invertebrates lost since 1970.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Some of the frightening figures there include 15 billion trees are being cut down each year and that more than half our rainforests are gone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Coral reefs, which also absorb heat, are dying at an alarming rate because of rising water temperatures and pollution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are also reports that 60% of invertebrates have been wiped out since 1970.

sections.label: Paying countries to conserve forests
sections.summary: The speaker proposes paying countries to conserve forests, funded by a price on pollution and carbon emissions, ideally via global carbon trading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In my view, the only sensible solution to this is that we have to pay countries to conserve their forests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And in order to make this payment, there must be a price on pollution and carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Ideally, if we can have a global carbon trading market, we may be able to have a fair system where countries that create carbon sinks to absorb carbon get payments for doing so, and countries that emit carbon pay for the same.

sections.label: Singapore's COVID-19 response measures
sections.summary: Singapore set up a Ministerial taskforce in January 2020, kept fatality rates low, and absorbed economic impact through emergency financial measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore anticipated the seriousness of this threat and set up its Ministerial taskforce as early as January 2020 with both strategy and tactics coordinated at a high level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the challenges, we have generally managed well and kept our fatality rate amongst the lowest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have also managed to absorb a large part of the economic impact because of the emergency financial measures we put in place – companies were supported in their payroll, rentals were reduced and managed, and workers who lost jobs or lost income were given compensation.

sections.label: Adequate vaccine supply
sections.summary: Singapore has an adequate supply of vaccines arriving during the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Happily, Singapore is in a position where we have adequate supply of the vaccines coming in the course of the year.

sections.label: Non-monetary vaccine incentives
sections.summary: The speaker suggests giving non-monetary incentives to vaccinated people, such as allowing groups larger than eight to meet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: My suggestion is a variation on the scheme but I would suggest that what we should do is give incentives to people who take the vaccine but not monetary incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, for example, if you have a group of people who are all vaccinated, they may be allowed to meet in groups of larger than eight.

sections.label: Budget costs and deficit
sections.summary: Five Budgets with COVID-19 support cost almost $100 billion, with Health at $18.8 billion and an $11 billion deficit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The last five Budgets with all the additional COVID-19 support measures have cost Singapore almost $100 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This year, our expenditure for Health has shot up to $18.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Defence will cost $15.4 billion and Education will cost $13.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Our deficit for this year is projected at $11 billion.

sections.label: Private property sales unsold units
sections.summary: Private property sales did not slow despite recession, and URA reports 52,783 unsold units with planning approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Sale of private properties by developers and in the resale market did not slow down at all despite this recession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And despite the fact that there are many unsold properties in the market, URA tells me that there are 52,783 unsold units in the market which have already obtained planning approval.

sections.label: Fiscal prudence and reserves
sections.summary: The speaker urges fiscal prudence and saving, noting car showroom crowds and that businesses can operate from anywhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Friends in the car industry also told me that there were visibly more people in the car showrooms looking to buy cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It was as if there was no recession at all, much less the worst recession in Singapore’s history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to continue to be fiscally prudent in its Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We need to save for another rainy day because we really have no other natural resources except our reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has changed the way many businesses operate and many businesses have realised that they can operate their business from anywhere in the world without having to come to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, we must never take Singapore’s continued success for granted.

sections.label: Working from home survey
sections.summary: 58% of firms would not endorse working from home, while 42% would, and the speaker suggests 40% of organisations commit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: About 58% said it would not and citing reasons such as lower productivity, majority of the staff are operational staff, lack of opportunities for building camaraderie, for not endorsing working from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The bright spot is that the remaining 42% said they would embrace working from home in the long run and they said about 20% of their staff would likely be working from home at any one time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: If this is representative of the majority of companies in Singapore, we could take the opportunity to re-shape our public transport system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I would go further and suggest that we actively work toward having about 40% of organisations in Singapore commit to having about 20% of their staff to work from home at any one time.

sections.label: Bus services profitability and subsidies
sections.summary: Of 356 bus services in 2019, only 11 were profitable, and the Government subsidised $1 billion for the remaining 345.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat also informed us that out of the 356 bus services in Singapore, only 11 services were profitable in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government had to subsidise $1 billion to operate the remaining 345 services.

sections.label: Bus 61 versus train travel time
sections.summary: Service 61 from Bukit Batok takes over two hours and calls at 19 MRT stations, while the train takes 46 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: For service 61, the bus ride from Bukit Batok takes more than two hours, calling on 19 MRT stations in between.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: If you take a train from Bukit Batok to Eunos, the travelling time is only 46 minutes – 120 minutes bus ride as compared to 46 minutes train ride.

sections.label: Proposal for CBD bus services
sections.summary: Most CBD buildings are within 400 metres of an MRT station, so LTA is urged to end buses outside the CBD and add feeder services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Most buildings in the CBD are within 400 metres of an MRT station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, I propose that LTA consider having bus services terminate at MRT station bus stops just outside the CBD and have dedicated feeder bus services to ply within CBD, connecting all the interchange MRT stations.

sections.label: Petrol tax cost for taxis
sections.summary: For taxis travelling 400 km a day, the additional $1 per litre petrol tax costs $663 more a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: For taxis that travel 400 km a day, the additional $1 per litre of petrol tax amounts to $663 additional cost a year.

sections.label: Extending COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund
sections.summary: As working from home continues, LTA is urged to extend the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund to the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The trend of working from home will continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge LTA to consider extending the COVID-19 Driver Relief Fund to the end of the year.

sections.label: Four additional Budgets and measures
sections.summary: The Government announced four additional Budgets with nearly $100 billion to help sectors, companies, workers, ventures and startups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To help the new rising companies and try to avoid the downfall of some big wigs, the Government has announced four additional Budgets with a supplement of nearly $100 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Budget will: one, help certain sectors to retain, retrain and prepare workers to be ready to spring back right away after recovery; two, help companies transform themselves for the future digital economy; three, support the core and the worst hit sectors, such as aviation, land transport, arts and sports; four, co-fund new ventures in the areas of creative ideas; and five, help the high-growth enterprises and the startups to have continued access into financial capital.

sections.label: Green bonds for infrastructure
sections.summary: Green bonds on selected public sector infrastructure projects are welcomed, and the speaker hopes MOF and MSE expand the scope of such projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The green bonds on selected public sector infrastructure projects is a welcomed financing tool to catalyse the flow of capital towards sustainable development and to anchor Singapore as a green finance hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng has announced that up to $19 billion of projects will be allocated towards developing our green economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So I hope MOF and MSE will expand the scope for such green infrastructure projects so as to accelerate the pace of achieving the targets set out in the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sections.label: Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes $60 million committed to a new Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund to help reach the 30-by-30 goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I have always felt strongly about ensuring food security for Singapore, so much so that I had urged the Government for more sector support in this House a few times in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the decision to commit $60 million to a new Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Fund will help us move towards the 30-by-30 goal of producing 30% of our food through local farms by 2030.

sections.label: Funding increase and APF question
sections.summary: The speaker seeks assurance that funding will increase when the economy recovers and asks if the Fund is additional to the 2014 APF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, I seek the Minister's assurance that funding will be increased when our economy recovers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Minister if the Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund is in addition to the $63 million Agriculture Productivity Fund (APF) launched in 2014.

sections.label: Locally sourced products and green bonds
sections.summary: Buying locally sourced and made products reduces carbon footprint, and the speaker supports issuing green bonds for select public infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Buying products using materials that are preferably locally sourced and made here is another way of reducing one's carbon footprint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I full-heartedly support the Ministry's decision to issue green bonds to fund select public infrastructure projects.

sections.label: Support for drivers on petrol duty
sections.summary: The speaker appeals for more support for motorcyclists, taxi and private-hire-car drivers, saying rebates will not offset higher petrol duty rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like to appeal on behalf of motorcyclists, taxi and private-hire-car drivers for more support to defray their increased cost of operations due to the increase in petrol duty rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While there are various measures to ease the transition, such as road tax rebates, cash handouts and petrol duty rebates, many of the users who depend on their vehicles for their livelihoods have shared with me their hardships and made their calculations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The rebates will not be enough to offset the higher duty rates.

sections.label: Drivers unable to switch to EVs
sections.summary: Drivers cannot yet switch to electric vehicles due to sunk costs or infrastructural constraints, and the hike will cut their take-home pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: They are not able yet to switch to electric vehicles due to sunk costs or infrastructural constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: They, however, are faced with the immediate reality that the hike will increase their costs and cut their take-home pay.

sections.label: Resident's shame over Singapore emissions
sections.summary: A speaker says a young resident, Brian, was ashamed to be Singaporean, citing rising emissions, high per capita emissions and a Climate Action Tracker red rating.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The idea that we can grow our environmental sustainability and our economy, both together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I was perturbed when a young resident, Brian, said to me that he was ashamed to be Singaporean, because we are not doing enough; that Singapore's emissions are still rising at 2% to 3%; that we are among the worst in the world in terms of emissions per capita; that on the Climate Action Tracker website, we are squarely in the Red zone, indicating that our policies and commitments are, I quote, "outside of (a country's) fair-share range and are not at all consistent with holding warming to below two degrees Celsius, let alone with the Paris Agreement's stronger 1.5 degree Celsius".

sections.label: Singapore share of global emissions
sections.summary: Singapore accounts for only 0.1% of global emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore accounts for only 0.1% of global emissions.

sections.label: Urban canyon and emissions ranking
sections.summary: The urban canyon effect in the CBD affects micro-level temperatures, and Singapore ranks 27th of 142 countries in emissions per capita.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While in our CBD, the "urban canyon" effect affects temperatures at the micro level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is true Singapore ranks 27th highest out of 142 countries in emissions per capita.

sections.label: Jurong Island oil and gas
sections.summary: Jurong Island hosts more than 100 oil, gas and petrochemical companies and over $50 billion in investments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Take Jurong Island – home to more than 100 oil and gas companies, and petrochemical companies, and investments of more than $50 billion.

sections.label: Shipping global greenhouse emissions
sections.summary: Shipping normally generates 2% of global greenhouse emissions and as a country would be the sixth largest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Normally shipping generates 2% of global greenhouse emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As a country it will be the sixth largest.

sections.label: ASEAN emissions and Indonesia share
sections.summary: The 10 ASEAN economies contribute 7.5% of global emissions, with Indonesia accounting for more than 60%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The 10 ASEAN economies contribute 7.5% of global emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The countries have very different carbon intensities, with Indonesia accounting for more than 60%.

sections.label: Inclusive transition green jobs
sections.summary: An inclusive transition must create new green jobs with training and reskilling so the most vulnerable benefit directly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: An inclusive transition must, therefore, create new green jobs, with training and reskilling, so that the most vulnerable will directly benefit.

sections.label: Green Economy jobs, Malay STEM gap
sections.summary: New Green Economy jobs will be created in engineering, carbon services and green financing, but the Malay community remains underrepresented in STEM.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: New jobs will be created in the new Green Economy, in fields like engineering, carbon services and green financing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Although our Malay community has made progress overall in tertiary education, we remain underrepresented in STEM fields.

sections.label: Helping Malays into STEM
sections.summary: Government, schools and M3 must help Malay youths and workers get an equal chance at STEM skills, including green technologies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government, schools and M3 must help Malay youths and Malays in the workforce to get an equal chance at developing interest, knowledge and skills in STEM, including green technologies.

sections.label: Travel bubbles and infrastructure investment
sections.summary: Singapore should pursue more travel bubbles with strategic countries and invest in long-term infrastructure against future pandemics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, we should look and work towards having more travel bubbles with strategic countries as the situation improves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, we have to invest in Singapore’s long-term infrastructure to prepare ourselves against future pandemics even after we see the end of this one, which may be another four to five years away.

sections.label: Social compact and Budget 2021
sections.summary: Budget 2021 focuses on strengthening the social compact through ComLink expansion, support for children with special needs and lower income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Their surroundings made them appreciate that they are all members of a collective and broadened their sense of identity, enabling them to see others as their own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am thus happy that Budget 2021 focuses on strengthening our social compact, with the expansion of ComLink, greater support for children with special needs and assistance to lower income households through various schemes.

sections.label: Agri-food fund for Keat Hong
sections.summary: Keat Hong hosts many local farms in Lim Chu Kang and Kranji, so the $60 million agri-food production fund is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Keat Hong is home to many of our local farms in Lim Chu Kang and Kranji.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, the $60 million fund to boost production in the agri-food sector is welcomed.

sections.label: Sustainable jobs, green financing, EV charging
sections.summary: A Sustainable Job Fair was held at Keat Hong CC, and the speaker proposes a green financing awareness campaign and EV charging legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last year, Keat Hong CC played host to a Sustainable Job Fair organised by South West CDC, SembCorp Industries and e2i.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It was the first-of-its kind sustainable jobs discovery in the heartlands and part of the South West CDC’s efforts to aggregate jobs in the growing sustainability sector, such as the solar and clean energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On green financing, I propose a public awareness campaign on the Singapore Green Plan and building strong partnerships with banks and investors in the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, on electric vehicles or EVs, as stated in my previous filed Parliamentary Question, we should not only look at the infrastructure, but also the legislation and regulatory framework to mandate possibly the installation of more EV charging stations in private residential and commercial carparks.

sections.label: Self-help groups and ethnic heritage
sections.summary: Self-help groups such as CDAC, SINDA, Mendaki and the Eurasian Association play important roles in keeping ethnic heritages alive in modern Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The self-help groups, such as CDAC, SINDA, Mendaki and the Eurasian Association, play important roles in keeping ethnic heritages alive in modern day Singapore.

sections.label: Ethnic Integration Programme in HDB estates
sections.summary: The Ethnic Integration Programme within HDB estates is cited as another example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Another example is the Ethnic Integration Programme within HDB estates.

sections.label: Singaporean first, ethnicity second
sections.summary: The speaker says the identity marker for his age group and younger is Singaporean first and ethnicity second, so leadership choice must be the best man regardless of race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I think the identity marker in my age group of Singaporeans and younger is: Singaporean first, and ethnicity second.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I think that means that when choosing a candidate to lead the Government, the choice must be the best man for the job, regardless of race.

sections.label: Wish on race and leadership
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore has some way to go and wishes that race is not used as a trump card or disqualifying criterion in choosing a Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe we have some way to go.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But my wish for Singapore is that, one day – perhaps when deciding the 5G or 6G Prime Minister – race is not used as a trump card or a disqualifying criterion.

sections.label: Best person for the job
sections.summary: The speaker argues it should be the best man, or best person, for the job regardless of race, and women should not be discounted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The point I am making in this speech is that it should be the best man for the job regardless of race, or dare I say the best person for the job regardless of race, for I do not see why a woman with outstanding leadership ability should be discounted.

sections.label: Adoption option for pregnant women
sections.summary: Speaker hopes couples wanting to adopt can connect with prospective mothers, and that MSF reports improved counselling on adoption for pregnant women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If we can create an environment in which couples who are unable to have their own children but who would love to have children and want to adopt can be placed in touch with the database of prospective mothers in Singapore, wanting to offer their babies for adoption, this would benefit both parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But for this to happen, the pregnant women must be told of this option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I have had discussions with MSF over many years and I hope they will close the loop with me and inform me how the counselling for pregnant women, to ensure that they are aware that adoption is a good and feasible option, has improved.

sections.label: Citizenship for stateless people
sections.summary: Speaker believes granting stateless people in Singapore citizenship or PR status would give them a rooted identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Today, I have spoken a lot of what it means to be Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe giving stateless people living in Singapore citizenship or at least PR status would go a long way in giving them something to be rooted in – the identity of being a citizen.

sections.label: Committed $100 billion
sections.summary: Last year, the speaker committed close to $100 billion to fight this crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, I committed close to $100 billion to fight this crisis.

sections.label: Global GDP and labour impact
sections.summary: Global real GDP fell an estimated 3.5% in 2020, with aviation, tourism and labour markets heavily disrupted.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Globally, real GDP is estimated to have fallen by 3.5% in 2020, equivalent to a drop of close to US$ 5 trillion dollars in economic output.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Sectors like aviation and tourism felt the brunt of the impact, with 1 billion fewer international arrivals in 2020 – a 74% drop.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Labour markets were disrupted on an unprecedented scale, with 8.8% of global working hours lost relative to the fourth quarter of 2019.

sections.label: Policy measures prevented contraction
sections.summary: Fiscal and monetary measures are estimated to have prevented 6.6 percentage points of GDP contraction and mitigated unemployment, with the rebound recouping about 80% of lost output.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our fiscal and monetary policy measures are estimated to have prevented a further 6.6 percentage points in GDP contraction last year, and mitigated the rise in resident unemployment rates by two percentage points – or about 155,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: While our economy contracted sharply in the second quarter of 2020, compared to the fourth quarter of 2019, the rebound over the next two quarters recouped about 80% of the output lost.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore financing schemes
sections.summary: In 2020, Enterprise Singapore's financing schemes supported $18 billion worth of loans to 21,000 enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In 2020, $18 billion worth of loans to 21,000 enterprises were supported by Enterprise Singapore's financing schemes.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills placements
sections.summary: Nearly 76,000 local jobseekers were placed in jobs and skills opportunities through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package from April to December last year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Nearly 76,000 local jobseekers were placed in jobs and skills opportunities through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package between April and December last year.

sections.label: Youth unemployment rate comparison
sections.summary: Youth unemployment rose two percentage points from September 2019 to September 2020 but stayed well below EU countries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: While unemployment rate amongst our young increased by two percentage points from September 2019 to September 2020, it remained well below that in EU countries.

sections.label: 2021 GDP growth forecast
sections.summary: The overall GDP growth forecast for 2021 is estimated at 4% to 6%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Overall, the GDP growth forecast for 2021 is estimated at 4% to 6%.

sections.label: Action plan for economic transformation
sections.summary: A $24 billion three-year action plan pursues medium to longer term economic imperatives, including $4.4 billion of the $8.3 billion Transformation and Growth strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa highlighted, our $24 billion action plan over the next three years is about pursuing our medium to longer term economic imperatives, even as we tackle the immediate challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will build an eco-system that fosters a virtuous cycle of innovation and knowledge transfer.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This includes $4.4 billion of the on-going $8.3 billion Transformation and Growth strategy I announced at the Unity Budget last year, to deepen enterprise capabilities and upskill workers.

sections.label: Productivity and median income growth
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2019 labour productivity and real median income grew faster than in the preceding three-year period, though 2020 saw 1.5% income growth and higher unemployment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2019, labour productivity growth, measured in terms of real value-added per actual hour worked, grew by 2.7% per year, up from 2.2% per year in the preceding three-year period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Real median income of Singaporeans increased by 3.7% per year, higher than the 3.2% per year growth in the preceding three-year period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Still, real median income of Singaporeans grew 1.5% year-on-year, while unemployment was higher in 2020 than in 2019.

sections.label: Biomedical manufacturing value-added growth
sections.summary: Since 2000, the value-added of the biomedical manufacturing sector has grown by more than three times.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since 2000, the value-added of the biomedical manufacturing sector has grown by more than three times.

sections.label: Support for smaller firms
sections.summary: In 2020, smaller firms received three to seven times more support per dollar of value-added than larger firms.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
